sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.1: A lot of Apotheosis is normally based on exploration. Recipes have been added for most things requiring exploration and mobs. You can have Godforged equipment without ever killing a mob or looting a Chest. You can of course have a mob farm or loot Nether Fortress Chests as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.2: Apotheosis usually requires a large amount of experience for things. You can use the Ender IO Experience Obelisk to store mass amounts of experience for later use. There is also an Enchanted Book called Knowledge of the Ages which converts enemy drops into experience. This scales with things like Looting and also Scavenger, which has a chance to roll a mobs drop table twice.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.5: Obtained by salvaging a Common affix item or Metal Mixture Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.6: Used in a Reforging Table to reforge equipment.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.8: Obtained by salvaging an Uncommon affix item, or made in an MV Chemical Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.9: Used in a Reforging Table to reforge equipment.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.11: Obtained by salvaging a Rare affix item, or made in an HV Chemical Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.12: Used in a Reforging Table to reforge equipment.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.14: Obtained by salvaging an Epic affix item, or made in an HV Chemical Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.15: Used in a Reforging Table to reforge equipment.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.17: Obtained by salvaging a Mythic affix item, or made in an EV Autoclave.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.18: Used in a Reforging Table to reforge equipment.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.20: There are 4 options for obtaining Gem Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.21: You can use the normal way of dropping an Anvil on some Apotheosis Gems.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.22: Once you have some you can craft a Salvaging Table which can also break down Gems or Metal Mixture Dust into Gem Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.23: You can run Metal Mixture Dust through a Macerator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.24: You can also craft Gem Dust in an HV Mixer with some rather basic materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.26: Apotheosis adds the ability to upgrade Spawners by using certain items on a Spawner. Most of the items required are GregTech related, see the uses for a Spawner in EMI to see the modification items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.27: Apotheosis also adds the ability to harvest Spawners using Silk Touch, however this does cause quite a bit of durability damage to the tool.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.28: Spawners are craftable and Spawn Eggs are purchasable from the Market block. You can use a Spawn Egg on a Spawner to set the Spawner to that mob type.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.31: Apootheosis greatly extends enchanting by increasing the maximum levels of enchantments. Enchanting Tables can now exceed level 30 enchantmnets by using certain Bookshelves from Apotheosis. You can see in the tooltip of an item which stats it will increase. If you max out Eterna you will be able to spent 100 levels on enchantments.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.34: Apotheosis adds the ability to add/remove affixes to/from items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.35: If you obtain an affix item, you can break it down into Rarity Materials. These Rarity Materials can be used to place affixes on your equipment.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.36: There are also Gems. Gems can be socketed into equipment if the equipment has an available socket space. This can be done in the Smithing Table.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.37: All Gems are craftable in the lowest tier they come in and can be upgraded from there.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.38: More information on these processes can be found below.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.41: Allows you to either add affixes to equipment or reroll the affixes that is already on a piece of equipment using experience, Gem Dust and Rarity Materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.42: No choices will be shown until you place a Rarity Material as that will determine which rarity the affix will be.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.43: The Simple Reforging Table has a maximum rarity of Rare, if you want higher tier rarities you need the Reforging Table.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.45: Works the same as the Simple Reforging Table but allows up to Mythic rarity.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.47: Insert unwanted affix items and you can break them down into Rarity Material of the same rarity.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.48: &6The item will be destroyed in the process.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.49: Note you can also craft all of the Rarity Materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.51: Can be used to add a gem socket to an item in a Smithing Table.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.53: Apotheosis is really only here for side stuff if you want, nothing is required at all to progress with GregTech. It was mostly only added to I could have really fast movement speed with affixes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.54: Stable Footing is also a great enchantment since we have flight from the start of the pack, which is also craftable in the Ender IO Enchanter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.57: Can be used to remove all gems from a socketed item in a Smithing Table.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.59: Using the Apothic Condenser multiblock you can craft base level Gems of every kind, and also upgrade them through the rarity tiers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.60: Basic gems are all crafted in the same manner, just using a different input of Exquisite Gem types from GregTech depending on the gem to craft.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.61: All Cracked Gems can be crafted using 120 EU/t and out of MV materials. Upgrading rarity tiers will start to cost more energy and use more expensive materials, but you can get to Perfect Gems in the IV age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.62: All rarity materials can be crafted while advancing through the GregTech ages as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_apotheosis.63: The Gem Cutting Table is disabled so this is the only way to upgrade them.

The ME Drive is what holds the Storage Cells, the Storage Cells are what actually store the items or fluids.
The standard ME Drive holds 10 Storage Cells. You can have multiple ME Drives to increase storage capacity. There is also an upgraded version that holds 20 Storage Cells.
You have a fully loaded ME Drive with 8 64k ME Item Storage Cells and 2 64k ME Fluid Storage Cells. You will most likely require more than 1 eventually though.
Under the ME Drive is a Creative Energy Cell.
You're welcome.

ME Drive
Insert Blank Patterns into the slot and encode crafting recipes into Blank Patterns for the Pattern Provider to use.

You can fill the grid with the required items from EMI like normal crafting recipes by pressing the [+] Fill Recipe button from the EMI recipe preview, or drag in specific items from the EMI right pannel for viewing items.

Keep in mind you do not technically require the recipe in the Pattern to be "accurate". Meaning you could say 1 Stick = 1 Cobblestone. While that example is pointless, this can be used to omit certain inputs that could be obtained from something else, as in a passive production of Rubber Sheets already pumps into a machine that will do the craft, so you could omit the Rubber Sheets from the Pattern and only state the items that the network needs to provide to complete the craft.
A crafting task is only ever marked as completed when the system receives the final result of the crafting Pattern.

For Processing Pattern you can middle click the input item to change the amount. If filling the Pattern grid from EMI this is usually not required, if manually setting up a Pattern you may need to state how many inputs are required.
Encoding Blank Patterns!
Provides Pattern ingredients to blocks that can craft with them. Face a Molecular Assembler to allow the Patterns for basic Crafting. Face a machine to allow processing Patterns.
Basic autocrafting just requires 1 of these containing a Pattern (up to 9) facing the block you want to craft with.

To register an autocraft as complete, the system needs to have the crafted items inserted back into the system, this block will work for that as anything inserted into it will be inserted back into the system.
There is an annoying quirk with GregTech machines,
There are more advanced Pattern Providers from addon mods that have a larger Pattern storage.
Like the Terminals, you can also make the smaller panel version that is not a full block.
Holds Patterns!
Performs Crafting Table recipes. Requires a Pattern Provider with a Crafting Pattern inside.
When you request a craft this is the block that will actually craft items for Crafting Patterns.
If using a Processing Pattern, this is not required.
Super crafter!
Used to create Printed Circuits and Processors, which are used for almost everything throughout AE2.
The Presses can be crafted as they are not found in the world.
Can also be used to crush Certus Quartz and Fluix Crystals into their Dust forms, although a GregTech Macerator is faster if you have access to one.
The start!
Inscriber \& Presses
Can be used to import or export item or fluids.
Set a filter above a slot to export that item or fluid from the network into the ME Interface.
Insert an item or fluid into a slot with no filter to insert into the network.
Typically used either to send item back into your system if you cant do so with the Pattern Provider for some reason, or to passively keep a machine stocked with an item or fluid.

For example, a Circuit Assembler always needs either Liquid Soldering Alloy or Liquid Tin and the input items. While the input items change from Circuit to Circuit, the fluid input does not. You can have an ME Interface constantly pump the fluid input into the Circuit Assembler while the Pattern only has the item inputs.
Like the Terminals, you can also make the smaller panel version that is not a full block.
Import/export!
The larger the Crafting Storage you have, the larger the recipes you can autocraft.
At least one of these are required anywhere in your network connection, they do not need to be near or connected to what is crafting the items at all.
There are higher tiers that allow more Crafting Storage, but you can also stack multiple Crafting Storages together to increase the size as well.

When you request a craft, you will see the "Crafting Plan" window open. This shows you how many of each input is required, as well as the "size" of the craft. The size is indicated in the top of the window where it says "Crafting Plan - X Bytes Used". The more things being crafted and being used to craft, the larger the size will be. If you don't have enough Crafting Storage available, you will not be able to request the craft.
Make the largest you can!
Crafting Storage
Crafting Storage
Can charge items with AE power (like Wireless Terminals), also used to charge Certus Quartz into a Charged Certus Quartz Crystal.
Note this cannot charge GregTech items with EU, GregTech has charging methods for that. Certain items requiring FE can be charged, but others may require a Charging Station.
Charging things!
Used in some recipes but mostly used to craft Fluix Crystals.

If you need to obtain Certus Quartz Crystals from AE2 (generally shouldn't need to) place a Certus Quartz from GregTech in an Autoclave with some Water. You can also use the toss in Water method that AE2 uses for other things like Fluix Crystals, just toss in a GregTech Certus Quartz and a Small Pile of Redstone Dust and it will convert to the AE2 version.
With access to the Certus Quartz Charger multiblock you can make Charged Certus Quartz Crystals much faster, and also use either version of Certus Quartz as well.
Either version will charge!
Fluix Crystals and Fluix Dust are used for many things throughout AE2.
Crafted by tossing Charged Certus Quartz Crystals, Redstone Dust, and Nether Quartz into a Water source block in the world, or they can also be made in a Mixer.
Water source block not consumed!
As you can see you have a functioning AE2 system with storage. There is a Creative Energy Cell under it all powering it. Your entire AE2 system will be free to use.
&nChannels are infinite.&r You are not limited by channels due to the mass amount of machines to deal with in GregTech. You can enable them in the AE2 configs if would like the added challenge.

No recipes have been changed for AE2 allowing a very easy start into the modpack. There has only been helper recipes added to help automate things and obtain world gen items like Press molds and Certus Quartz Crystals. You can also craft a Creative Energy Cell, in case you want separate networks, and no it cannot power anything else other than AE2.

Multiple addon mods are also present to allow much more AE2 expansion and interaction, as well as a few custom multiblocks like the Large Inscriber which takes all raw inputs and outputs finished Processors very quickly, and the Certus Quartz Charger which does as you would think, just very quickly and in bulk.
Not even close to everything will be included in this chapter, just the basics for getting a starter autocrafting setup.
&6With almost every item from AE2 you can hover your mouse over it and hold [G] to open an in game guide.&r
A quick note!
A Note on AE2
Applied Energistics 2

Can access your AE2 system wirelessly from your inventory. Requires energy to use, and can be equipped in a Curio slot. A decent way to charge it early on is by using a Basic/Advanced Wireless Player Charger, hide one under your floor of a main part of your base and as you are near it will charge it while it's equipped.
To link it to your network you need to have a ME Wireless Access Point somewhere on your network. Insert the Wireless Crafting Terminal in the top left slot and it will link it to that network.
The default wireless range is not great being 32 blocks, but you can increase it by placing Wireless Boosters in the ME Wireless Access Point. They stack and increase the range bit by bit.
You can also use a Quantum Bridge Card to make the range infinite and allow wireless charging from your network. See the related quests to the left for the Quantum Ring and the Quantum Bridge Card.
Access your system from your inventory!
A multiblock that can produce 4 Charged Certus Quartz Crystals at a time very quickly.
The base time is 0.8 seconds and this can be cut in half by providing Nitrogen Gas.
Accepts both AE2 and GregTech Certus Quartz.
Multiblock Charger!
Certus Quartz Charger (M)
A multiblock version of the Inscriber. Makes finished Processors very fast out of base materials and non consumable press molds.

Cable Facades can be placed on AE2 Cables to hide the cable and make it look like another block.
The recipes are hidden in EMI because there are so many of them. Simply craft 4 Cable Anchors around any block in a crafting grid and you will craft 4 Cable Facades of that block type.
Note that GregTech also has Facades, they are used for GregTech Cables only.
There are also Facades from the Cable Facades mod, which can be used on basically any mod in the pack.

Cable Facade
The Quantum Ring is a small multiblock that allows for wireless transfer through the network.
It is constructed by making a square of 8 ME Quantum Rings with an ME Quantum Link Chamber in the center. You will need this setup for both the sending and receiving locations.
If placed correctly you will see the blocks form into a multiblock. Plug a Cable into the sending location to see the device online.
Then you will need 2 Quantum Entangled Singularities, 1 for each Quantum Ring setup. Insert 1 into each ME Quantum Link Chamber. This is what links the 2 setups together.
Now you can run a Cable from the receiving location and it will be connected to the same network.

To obtain the 2 Quantum Entangled Singularities that are linked to each other you must drop a Singularity and either an Ender Pearl or Ender Pearl Dust in the world and blow them up. This will convert the 1 Singularity into 2 Quantum Entangled Singularities (meaning they share the same frequency). Note that normal TNT has a process to make, Tiny TNT will also work and is rather basic to craft.
You can use these to travel infinite distances, access your Cleanroom, and even other dimensions.
Wireless AE2 Links!
Quantum Ring (M)
Now that you understand the Quantum Ring and Quantum Entangled Singularities, there is the Quantum Bridge Card.
This can be inserted into your Wireless Terminals to provide a wireless charge and infinite range.

For it to work you will also need a Quantum Entangled Singularity in a Quantum Ring, and the other in the special slot inside your Wireless Terminal which is between the "View Cells" and "Magnet Card" slots on the right of the GUI.

There is quite a bit to read here but if you do not know about AE2 Crafting CPUs, you should probably read through this.

AE2 uses what they call a "Crafting CPU" when doing any autocrafting tasks. If you search EMI for that, you won't find anything. They are technically either a single block or a multiblock that consist of 1 or more elements.
A Crafting CPU can be anywhere as long as it is connected to the network. They do not need to be anywhere near things being crafted, just connected to the same network.

The first and only technically required piece is a &2Crafting Storage&r. They come in multiple sizes, but technically only 1 Crafting Storage is required to be considered a Crafting CPU, however there are more things that can enhance capabilities, and you can also stack multiple Crafting Storages together to increase the size.

Another optional piece is the &2Crafting Co-Processing Unit&r. This allows a Pattern Provider to send out more ingredients faster when doing a crafting task. You can have more than 1 Crafting Co-Processing Unit, allowing for many things to be done in tandem if multiple machines are involved or if a machine processes things very quickly.
Another optional piece is the &2Crafting Monitor&r. This is just a way to see what the Crafting CPU is currently doing. You would only ever have 1 of these per Crafting CPU.

Another optional piece is the &2Crafting Unit&r. While it is a base crafting component for the other pieces, it can also be used to fill in spots in the Crafting CPU to make it the right shape if you don't have enough other blocks to fill it in, more on that below.

A Crafting CPU &6must be a certain shape&r in order to be functional, but it is rather flexible. A single block of just a Crafting Storage is valid. 2 blocks touching in any direction is valid. But when 3 or more blocks are together there are some conditions. Basically the structure must be a rectangular prism of some kind. 3 blocks in an L shape will not form. It must be some kind of square or rectangle to be considered valid. You will see the blocks change textures when in a valid form.

The final thing to mention is that each crafting task uses a Crafting CPU. Requesting 1 or 1000 of a single item type will still use 1 Crafting CPU, just the size of the crafting plan will change. If you want to request 10 Iron Plates and 10 Iron Gears, each crafting task needs a Crafting CPU. This being said, having just one Crafting CPU is not ideal.
What is a Crafting CPU?
"Crafting CPUs"
The ME Extended Drive is just a direct upgrade from the standard ME Drive, holding 20 Storage Cells instead of 10.
Functionally they are the exact same, they just hold more.
Up to 20 Storage Cells!
Pretty simple blocks, the ME Import Bus will import things into the system, while the ME Export Bus will export things from the system.
You can set filters in the GUI, and insert Acceleration Cards to increase the speed at which they import or export.

For lag purposes, if they have not done anything in a few seconds they will enter a slow mode, then pick back up to full speed when interacted with again. So if constantly interacting with something, the speed will remain normal and you should see instant results. But if something is only being interacted with every few seconds or longer, you may see a delay before it activates. Normally there is 4 operations per second. The number of items interacted with per operation can be increased with Acceleration Cards.
ME Import \& Export Buses
AE2 uses "Upgrade Cards" that can be installed in most devices to either change or enhance how they work. The tooltip of an Upgrade Card will state what devices it can be installed in, and how many.
There are Basic Cards and Advanced Cards, which can be crafted into different Upgrade Cards.
The Basic Card can be used to craft the following:
Redstone Card
Capacity Card
Overflow Destruction Card
Crafting Card
As there are many Upgrade Cards and multiple things they can do, see the in game AE2 guide for each Upgrade Card if you need more info by hovering over the Upgrade Card and holding [G] by default.
Not for Acceleration Cards!

Fuzzy Card
Acceleration Card

Greater Energy Card
Magnet Card

As there are many Upgrade Cards and multiple things they can do, see the in game AE2 guide for each Upgrade Card if you need more info by hovering over the Upgrade Card and holding [G] by default.
For Acceleration Cards!

A Matter Condenser is basically what it sounds like, it condenses matter to either create a Singularity or a Matter Ball. While Matter Balls don't see much practical use, a Singularity does, and EMI can look a bit misleading on how to make them.
The Matter Condenser has 3 modes, and be careful as the default mode is literally a trash can that voids anything you put in it.
The second mode is for making Matter Balls, and the third mode is for making Singularities.
To make a Singularity, first set it to the correct mode. Then you will need to input a 64K ME Storage Component or higher, however a 256K will not provide any benefit.

The Matter Condenser will accept items or fluids and "condense" the inputs into a Singularity. A single Singularity will take 256,000 items or buckets of fluid to make. This will not consume the ME Storage Component in the process.

While a Singularity does have more than one use, they are mostly used for Quantum Entangled Singularites used with the Quantum Ring. The Quantum Ring quest below will explain that, but basically just blow up the Singularity with either an Ender Pearl or Ender Pearl Dust to get 2 linked Quantum Entangled Singularities.
If you need a lot of Singularities, look into the Expanded IO Port + ME Infinity Water Cell to push directly into the Matter Condenser at incredibly fast speeds.
Compressing matter!
The Quantum Computer is a multiblock Crafting CPU that can have a very large amount of storage and many co-processing threads.

To make the most basic version all you need is the Quantum Computer Core and 26 Quantum Computer Structural Glass. This will be a 3*3*3 of the Quantum Computer Structural Glass with the Quantum Computer Core in the center. This will give a Crafting CPU with 256M crafting storage and 8 co-processing threads.
The maximum size can be 7*7*7, there are more blocks you can add inside for additional capabilities.

The Quantum Computer must have exactly 1 Quantum Computer Core, and all outside faces must be the Quantum Computer Structural Glass. There cannot be any empty spaces inside, and the inside cannot contain any Quantum Computer Structural Glass. The Quantum Computer Core inside will change shape and texture when it forms correctly, and when it has power the edges of the Quantum Computer Structural Glass will glow.
128M and 256M Quantum Computer Storages will increase the total crafting storage of the Quantum Computer.
A Quantum Data Entangler will multiply the total crafting storage of the Quantum Computer by 4. &6Limited to 1 per Quantum Computer.&r
Quantum Accelerators will add 8 co-processing threads to the Quantum Computer.
A Quantum Computer Multi-Threader will multiply the total co-processing threads by 4. &6Limited to 1 per Quantum Computer.&r
Quantum Crafting Units can be used to fill empty spaces within the multiblock, but have no added features, they are just a base crafting block that can be used to fill void space as well.
The most basic 3*3*3 setup.
Advanced AE!
Quantum Computer

The EU P2P Tunnel allows you to send EU through your AE2 network. It still follows normal GregTech rules as in feeding a higher voltage to lower tier machines and Cables will blow up the machines and burn up the Cables.

To attune the P2P Tunnel to EU, use any GregTech Wire Cutters (does not need to be a powered version) on the basic ME P2P Tunnel. You can also just craft them from any P2P Tunnel in an Assembler with a Programmed Circuit value. This goes for all P2P Tunnels.
They do not transform voltage tiers, they just act as if there was no gap between the 2 EU P2P Tunnels.

Note that the EU Multi P2P Tunnels do not act as intended with GregTech Cables or Wires in play. Using EU Multi P2P Tunnels attached directly to sources and destinations works, but if any Cables or Wires are being used, they do not work as intended. A normal EU P2P Tunnel can interact with Cables or Wires fine though.

There is also some issues interacting with things like Transformers and multiple standard Energy Hatches in a single multiblock. A Battery Buffer before a Transformer or Energy Hatches seems to get around the issue, and using multiple multi amp Energy Hatches appear to work fine compared to multiple standard Energy Hatches.

While they can be a bit stubborn sometimes, technically you wouldn't ever need Superconductors for EU transfer, just for recipes that require them, which are typically not required until IV Field Generators.
EU through AE!
EU P2P Tunnels
Modern AE2 Additions is an addon mod for AE2 that has larger Crafting Co-Processing Units from 4x to 256x, some additional P2P Tunnels, and a few other things.
Besides the larger Crafting Co-Processing Units, the EU P2P Tunnels are most likely the go to for this mod.

They work as you would expect, sending EU through the AE2 network. They do follow GregTech energy rules as in voltage tiers must match or things will explode or burn. They do not transform voltage tiers, they just act as if there was no gap between the 2 EU P2P Tunnels.
EU P2P \& more!
Modern AE2 Additions

Advanced AE offers a highly modular set of armor. Upgrades can be applied using Upgrade Cards which are all crafted from the Quantum Upgrade Base Card. The armor set is rather expensive to make but it can do quite a bit with all the Upgrade Cards.
In order to install Upgrade Cards you need to be wearing the armor and use the keybind (set in options) then select the piece of armor you are wearing.
To link an armor piece to your network, do the same as a Wireless Terminal, just insert it in the top right slot in an ME Wireless Access Point.

Each piece of armor will say in the tooltip what it can accept. The chestplate has a default effect of negating the mining speed penalty when flying. The boots have a default effect of negating fall damage.
As there are many upgrades available, some to note would be ME Recharging, Night Vision, Flight, Walk/Sprint Speed, Reach, Step Assist, and Flight Drift.

While flight is already obviously usable from the Angel Ring, the Flight Drift Card cancels the "gliding" effect when trying to stop in the air, like the inertia cancelling effect from the Draconic Evolution set. In order for the Flight Drift Card to take effect, you also need the Flight Card.
The ME Recharging Card will charge each armor piece it is installed in from the network, and if installed in the chestplate, it will also charge inventory items (not GregTech items unfortunately).
Highly modular armor set!
Quantum Armor
A Pattern Provider with this card inserted will change the Circuit number instead of pushing a Programmed Circuit into GregTech machines.

Include the Programmed Circuit in the Pattern. It will work even if there is no Programmed Circuit in the network. Manually placing it every time is inconvenient, so the behavior has been modified to include the Programmed Circuit when registering recipes from EMI.
Place the Programmed Circuit Card in the upgrade slot of the Pattern Provider. &6Don't forget to set the Pattern Provider to blocking mode.&r
Note: Blocking modes may not work well if multiple Pattern Providers are adjacent to one machine.
The Programmed Circuit will not appear in the crafting plan. If it does appear, check whether the Programmed Circuit Card is installed in the Pattern Provider.
&aSupports Pattern Providers from most AE2 addon mods.&r
Automatically set machine Circuit values!
The same as a normal Pattern Provider, but has 72 Pattern slots.
The Expanded Pattern Provider Upgrade can upgrade a basic AE2 Pattern Provider into an Expanded Pattern Provider in world while keeping the Patterns inside.
72 Pattern slots!
Can be used to pickup most AE2 block entities while preserving their settings and inventories.
Great for moving Pattern Providers and ME Drives.
Has durability but can be enchanted with Unbreaking and Mending.
Easily move things!
If attached to your AE2 network, when quest related items enter the network they will be detected for quests. Saving you having to physically hold the items.
Makes it easier to just automate all results into the network and not have to pull them back out just for the quests.
The same as the ME Level Emitter, however you can set a minimum and maximum quantity.
With this you can choose to send the redstone signal when you drop below a certain quantity and stop when you reach a certain quantity.
As normal you can invert the redstone behavior with the GUI button on the left.

Very helpful for many things, like a Fusion Reactor for producing plasma fuels. You can set it to turn on a Fusion Reactor when fluid levels of your fuel storage drop to a certain quantity (like 3000 buckets), and turn off when it reaches a higher quantity (like 3995 buckets). This really helps not having the Fusion Reactors flickering on and off constantly as small amounts of fuel are being consumed.
Obviously useful in many other scenarios but that is one practical example you can take the logic from.
Redstone signal based on threshold storage levels!

The ME Threshold Export Bus mostly works the same as the ME Export Bus, but you can set minimum or maximum quantities of the item or fluid that must be required in the network in order to export the item or fluid.
You set the item or fluid to export as normal in the filter slots, but then you can give it a threshold quantity by middle clicking on the filter slot.
You can set the ME Threshold Export bus to only be active when the system can see either less than or more than that set threshold quantity.
Use the button on the left side of the GUI to swap between above or below threshold settings.

For example you can have it export Ruthenium Dust, but only when you have at least 500 Ruthenium Dust available in the system, leaving you some left for other things in your storage so you don't export it all.
Export based on storage levels!
The ME Level Emitter is simple and helpful.
You can set an item or fluid for it to read from your system, and a quantity.
On the left there is a toggle button to swap between emitting a signal when either below or above the set quantity.
This can be used to easily turn things off and on based on storage levels, very helpful for controlling passive setups that can automatically turn off based on how much of something is available.
If using with GregTech machines, the machine will need a Machine Controller Cover installed to be able to accept redstone signals.
Redstone signal based on storage levels!

sky_greg.quests.chapters_circuit_process: This overview page will show mostly everything to do with Circuit Lines, Boules, Wafers, and Chips.
Visual indicators will be present for most things to help see things at a glance.
Depending on the plastic sheet you use, you can make more Plastic Circuit Boards at once with the same amount of other inputs.
A Polyethylene Sheet makes 1, a Polyvinyl Chloride Sheet makes 2, a Polytetrafluoroethylene Sheet makes 4, and a Polybenzimidazole Sheet makes 8.
They do take 25 seconds in an LV Chemical Reactor, so you may want to make at least a small passive stock, or scale up the setup, or overclock the Chemical Reactor when you can.
While the next tier of Circuit Board does need Liquid Epoxy, they are not a direct upgrade to the Epoxy Circuit Board.

The Fiber-Reinforced Circuit Board is obviously used to make the Fiber-Reinforced Printed Circuit Board, but is also used to make the Multi-layer Fiber Reinforced Circuit Board, which is also used to make the Wetware Circuit Board, so this is going to be needed for quite a while going forward.
Basically everything after this requires a Cleanroom!
MV Cutter/Laser Engraver | Light Blue/Diamond Lens
MV Cutter/Laser Engraver | Light Blue/Diamond Lens
EV Cutter/EV Chemical Reactor | No Lens
Wetware Circuit Board \& Neuro Processing Unit

The typical chain for Boules to Chips is normally EBF to make the Boule -> Cutter to make blank Wafers ->  Laser Engraver to make engraved Wafers -> Cutter to make Chips. There are a few types that don't quite follow this pattern and instead upgrade other Wafers. Anything requiring above an MV machine will also require a Cleanroom.
Higher tier Boules cut into more Wafers of that type.
Different engraved Wafers have a minimum tier of Wafer they can be made with, but engraving a Wafer with a higher tier Wafer than required will produce more engraved Wafers.
For example, making a CPU Wafer from a Silicon Wafer will make 1 CPU Wafer, and making a CPU Wafer from a Naquadah-doped Wafer will make 8 CPU Wafers.
The cutting of the engraved Wafers into Chips is always the same though.
For these reasons, it is always much more efficient to use higher tier Boules when you get access to them.
Once you get a Cleanroom, get in the habbit of making all your Laser Engraver and Cutter setups in the Cleanroom as basically everything is done in there once you have access to the Cleanroom.
The most used Chip by far!
There are multiple tiers of what is known as an SoC, System on Chip. Each tier of Wafers has a SoC for that tier that can be used in higher tier Circuit lines.

These are generally never required to make any Circuits, but if you do use the SoC recipes, they usually replace all the other Circuit components like Diodes, Capacitors, and such, while also crafting more Circuits, and are faster recipes. They also require a higher voltage tier of Circuit Assembler than the normal recipes.
You generally unlock access to the SoC for a Circuit type later on and can't start making the Circuits with them initially.
They also usually only make the starting Circuit of the Circuit line.
Universal Circuits basically have a single purpose, making autocrafting recipe management easier.
They are very cheap to make and are tagged as Circuits of the same tier, meaning you can use an LV Universal Circuit for anything an LV Circuit of any other kind can be used for.

Use the Universal Circuits in AE2 Patterns instead of normal Circuits, and when you upgrade your Circuits, you just need to change the Pattern for the Universal Circuit, instead of a bunch of machine recipes that use Circuits.
You can use either Raw Carbon Fibers or Borosilicate Glass Fibers to make the Reinforced Epoxy Resin Sheet.

Raw Carbon Fibers are made in an Autoclave with Carbon Dust and either Liquid Polyethylene, Liquid Polytetrafluoroethylene, Liquid Polybenzimidazole, or Liquid Expoxy. The higher tier of fluid used, less fluid is required and more Carbon Fibers are made.

Borosilicate Glass Fibers are actually quite easy to make, it's just 7 Glass Dust and 1 Boron Dust to make 8 Borosilicate Glass Dust in an LV Mixer, or an ABS to make Liquid Borosilicate Glass. You make 8 Borosilicate Glass Fibers in an LV Wiremill with 1 Borosilicate Glass Bar. So 1 batch makes 64 Borosilicate Glass Fibers in total at the cost of 7 Glass Dust and 1 Boron Dust.
Either way is viable but the Borosilicate Glass Fibers are more efficient.
Raw Carbon Fibers or Borosilicate Glass Fibers
Going forward for every Printed Circuit Board, you will either need Iron III Chloride, or Sodium Persulfate.

The amount required is always twice as much if using Sodium Persulfate. You might want to go the Iron III Chloride route. early on the difference doesn't seem like much to worry about, but by the time you get to the Wetware Printed Circuit Boards, it's a difference of 5000 mB of Iron III Chloride or 10,000 mB of Sodium Persulfate which really starts to add up on large crafts or passive setups.
Iron III Chloride uses Hydrochloric Acid, and Sodium Persulfate uses Sulfuric Acid. Hydrochloric Acid is easier to make early on compared to Sulfuric Acid.
&dTo make Iron III Chloride:&r you need 3000 mB Hydrochloric Acid and 1 Iron Dust to make 1000 mB Iron III Chloride and 3000 mB Hydrogen Gas.
To make Hydrochloric Acid in a very simple way, you need 2 Rock Salt and 1000 mB Water in an MV Chemical Reactor to make 3 Potassium Hydroxide Dust and 1000 mB Hydrochloric Acid.
&dTo make Sodium Persulfate:&r you need 7 Sodium Bisulfate Dust in an LV Electrolyzer to make 500 mB Sodium Persulfate and 1000 mB Hydrogen Gas.
To make Sodium Bisulfate you need 2 Salt and 1000 mB Sulfuric Acid in an LV Chemical Reactor to make 7 Sodium Bisultate Dust and 1000 mB Hydrochloric Acid.

To make Sulfuric Acid in a direct easy way, you need an LCR, if you don't have an LCR you should probably avoid the Sodium Persulfate route as other methods of making Sulfuric Acid are available, but just using 1 Sulfur Dust and 4000 mB Water to make 1000 mB Sulfuric Acid is really the only method worth doing unless you require one of the other methods earlier on.

GregTech uses a special energy system called EU that generally does not interact with FE. They can be converted between each other at a 1:4 ratio though. 1 EU = 4 FE.

GregTech also uses something called Amperage, or amps for short. An amp is basically a channel for an electrical current. You cannot just add 4 LV Steam Turbines together that are producing 32 EU/t to reach 128 EU/t. Instead you will end up with 4 amps of 32 EU/t. Wires/Cables and machines also have an amp rating. Single Block machines are usually only able to accept 1 amp of energy. Supplying too much EU/t or amps to a Wire/Cable will make them burn up and supplying too much EU/t to a machine will casuse the machine to explode.
It is very important to know how much energy you are sending to have the proper sized cables and proper tier of machines.

FE works completely differently, if you had 4 generators all producing 60 FE/t, you would end up just adding the numbers together and you would be producing 240 FE/t. There are no amps or electrical channels when it comes to FE.

You can convert between the 2 using an Energy Converter, be sure to match the tier of the EU you require with the right tier Energy Converter as there is one for each voltage tier. Check the tooltip of the Energy Converter to see the conversion rates and tiers.

You can stay completely with EU and use only GregTech if you wish, or you could convert FE generated using Advanced Genertors, however this would not be available until the IV age. If you wish to transfer your energy as FE you could generate EU, convert it to FE, transfer the FE wirelessly using a few methods like a Tesseract, then convert back to EU where you require it. This makes it so you could make a central bank of energy as FE and wirelessly transmit it where you need EU and convert it on site.
Burns liquids and gasses to generate FE. All fuels from the Gas Turbines and Combustion Generators have been added.
Burns Steam to generate FE. Steam from GregTech or Advanced Generators is acceptable.
Burns Carbon to generate Syngas, which can be burned in a Gas Turbine Controller

sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.80: As a comparison, the boosted recipe uses &a62.5% less Oxygen and 25% less Ethylene&r overall than the standard recipe at the cost of a bit of Titanium Tetrachloride.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.81: The other fluids all use the same quantities.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.82: These are LV recipes in the LCR that take 40 seconds, so running it at HV only takes 2.5 seconds due to the perfect overclock with the LCR.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.83: Also you make Titanium Tetrachloride at twice the rate that you use it for making Hot Titanium Ingots, so you would naturally have an excess of Titanium Tetrachloride with 1 LCR and 1 EBF with both running at HV. Also with the perfect overclock on the LCR, tiering up both the LCR and EBF to EV would mean even more excess Titanium Tetrachloride.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.87: Used to process recipes with an HV requirement.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.94: While you can make Cracked fuels in a Chemical Reactor, it halves the output quantity compared to the input quantity. The Cracker gives the full amount.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.99: Used to craft HV Energy Hatches and HV Dynamo Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.106: A basic alloy made from 4 Nickel Dust and 1 Chromium Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.107: Process Nickel Dust and Chromium Dust in an MV Mixer to produce Nichrome Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.108: Process in an EV EBF to produce Hot Nichrome Ingots.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.110: Mostly used to make Coils but it has some other uses.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.112: The HV Superconductor, has a loss of 0 EU per block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.114: A multiblock version of the Chemical Reactor, commonly referred to as the LCR. While it can process anything that a normal Chemical Reactor can, it also has some special recipes that can only be processed in the Large Chemical Reactor, like Iridium Metal Residue.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.115: Some recipes with multiple Chemical Reactor steps can be condensed into 1 recipe in the Large Chemical Reactor to skip processing steps, this is usually anything with the circuit value of 24 in the recipe, like Sulfuric Acid from just Water + Sulfur Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.116: Can be overclocked with 2 Energy Hatches, and has a perfect overclock, which uses less time and in turn total EU than a normal overclock. See the Perfect Overclocking quest for more information if needed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.119: The Multi Smelter is a very fast Furnace/Alloy Smelter multiblock.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.120: The speed will depend on the tier of Energy Hatches used, and the amount it processes at once will depend on the tier of Coils you use.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.121: Using Cupronickel Coils and 2 MV Energy Hatches it will perform 32 recipes at once in 3.2 seconds.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.122: You can change the "Active Machine Mode" in the GUI by clicking the button that looks like a Robot Arm. This will allow you to change between Electric Furnace and Alloy Smelter recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.125: Many people get confused of what a "perfect overclock" means. First let's start with the standard overclock mechanics.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.126: Overclocking a recipe is essentially what running a lower tier recipe at a higher tier is called. As in if a recipe requires an MV machine and you run it in an HV machine, the recipe duration is half of what is should normally be and the total EU used is double.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.127: For example, take a recipe that requires MV and takes 20 seconds and 24,000 total EU. If you run that recipe in an HV machine, it becomes 10 seconds, and 48,000 total EU. This is a standard overclock.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.128: Now if that was using a perfect overclock, it would be 5 seconds, and 24,000 total EU. You retain the normal total EU being used by cutting the time by 4 instead of 2.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.129: Note that the total EU does not change, the EU/t does x4 and the duration does /4.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.130: Single block machines will never do a perfect overclock. Not all multiblocks will either, only some that are specified to do so. The Large Chemical Reactor is one, anything from the "Large Series" multiblocks available in the IV age, and some from a custom "Perfect Series" of multiblocks available in the EV age, although the Large Series are significantly better than the Perfect Series overall as they allow Parallel Hatches, and 2 Energy Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.131: You can see the differences in the recipe previews by toggling the recipe tier by standard or perfect overclocking for a visual example.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.134: Radon Gas is used for quite a bit going forward, mostly in the form of Quantum Eyes and Quantum Stars, both of which are heavily used in high tier Sensors, Emitters, and Field Generators.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.135: While more ways to obtain open up later, the first route is still probably one of the more efficient ways.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.136: Plutonium is surprisingly just smelted from Plutonium Ores, and while you do get your Plutonium Dust back in the process, you could smelt it again and loop it around, or it may be simpler to just trash it and have a steady smelting process feeding into the LCR.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.137: The Air is pretty self explanitory, and the Uranium Dust actually has a couple options.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.138: If you want/need a lot of Uranium Dust (has more uses down the road), then without a doubt do the full processing line setup. If you just want a bit to get by, you can skip the process with an HV Macerator (at least) and a bunch of Red Granite. The chance is very low, but possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.142: The Glass Box is a multiblock that can make most Glass block types, all the dyed Lenses, Liquid Glass, and quite a few other Glass related things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.143: It uses Sand as a base, a bit of Oxygen Gas, and usually an additive or a Casting Mold.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.144: The additives required are usually in Dust form if possible, and always has a boosted output.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.145: The dyed Lenses just use the base Dyes, they do not require the Chemical Dyes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.146: It can accept a Parallel Hatch, but you can't quite get one until late IV.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.149: The Forming Press has some odd uses, mostly relating to Glass, Turbine Blades, and copying Extruder/Casting Molds, but is not really widely used. However Laminated Glass is required for things later on, and this is the only way to obtain it to start.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.150: You can make the Laminated Glass in the Glass Box multiblock, but the Glass Box still requires Laminated Glass to make.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.152: If you hadn't noticed by now, there are tiers of Glass used in recipes. Glass was tier 1, Tempered Glass was tier 2, and Laminated Glass is tier 3.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.153: Later on Fusion Glass will be tier 4, which is also made from Laminated Glass.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.154: Used in quite a few crafting recipes, and most notably to build the Power Substation and Assembly Line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.156: While an Eye of Ender may not seem immediately useful, they are required for HV Emitters, which are used in HV Laser Engravers and EV Circuit Assemblers. They are used for Quantum Eyes as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.157: Both the Eye of Ender and Quantum Eye are used in Field Generators, Sensors, and Emitters.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.158: There is no Stronghold, don't worry...
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.159: The End is a void dimension as well but it still has and End Island and Ender Dragon.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.160: There is no Stronghold. Craft an End Painting. If using Paintings for travel, remember to bring an Overworld Painting with you to get back as they do not create a return. You can also just use /home if you set your home at your base with /sethome.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.161: The only reason you will probably need to go here is for Ender Air. An Enderman farm wouldn't hurt to have either, but there are other means of obtaining Ender Pearls.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.162: You have to &njump&r into the Painting.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.165: The Auto Maintenance Hatch is as it sounds, it automatically deals with maintenance issues, meaning you don't have to.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.166: This essentially removes any maintenance issues.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.168: The second tier of Wafer material.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.169: An HV Cutter in a Cleanroom is required to cut the Boule.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.170: Cuts into 32 Phosphorus-doped Wafers at a time and better output ratios for Laser Engraving than the first tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.172: Requires an HV Cutter in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.173: Not only goes the Boule cut into more Raw Wafers, but the Laser Engraver step also produces more Engraved Wafers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.174: Requires an HV Laser Engraver in a Cleanroom to process into Engraved Wafers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.176: Flux Networks is all about wireless energy transfer. &6The Flux Storage blocks have been disabled&r so it can not be used to store energy, but it can be used to transfer energy and wireless inventory charging.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.178: Everything is handled within the GUI of the blocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.179: Create a network and assign the Flux Controller, Flux Plugs, and Flux Points to the same network. If a Flux Plug is receiving energy and a Flux Point is on the same network, it will wirelessly transfer from the Flux Plug to the Flux Point.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.180: They are expensive because they are powerful.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.182: - Used to allow wireless charging of items in your inventory.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.183: - Not required for just energy transfer.
