sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.191: Uses the same logic and recipes as the normal EBF, but can run 4 parallels with a reduced total EU cost and slightly higher EU/t cost.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.196: While it uses a bit more than normal EU/t when running parallels, it still uses less EU overall than running 4 standard recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.197: Can accept up to 3 Energy Hatches to allow more EU for the higher EU/t costs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.198: It will run with less than 4 inputs available, so if you want to force the parallels, make sure to input in batches of 4. This can be done in a few ways but the easiest way is to just make your patterns be set to 4 inputs = 4 outputs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.199: 4 parallels \& less total EU than 4 EBFs!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.202: In order to start powering EV machines, you are going to require either a High Voltage Transformer or an EV Battery Buffer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.203: As single block generators are no longer available from EV and up, and the EV Dynamo Hatch requires EV machines, you need a way to get an EV voltage without an EV generator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.204: Transformers can be used to either step up 4 amps of a lower voltage tier to 1 amp of a higher voltage tier, or step down 1 amp of a higher voltage tier to 4 amps of a lower voltage tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.205: It starts in Transform Down mode, use a Screwdriver to change the mode.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.206: The standard version allows 4 amps in and 1 amp out, or 1 amp in and 4 amps out, depending on the transfer mode.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.207: There are 2x, 4x, and 16x versions as well, which allow for more amps in and out.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.208: You could also make an EV Battery Buffer and some EV Batteries instead. They do not require any EV machines to make, and you can power EV Batteries inside an EV Battery Buffer with lower voltage generators. This may not be the ideal method, but it is possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.209: You can either draw the EU from the Battery Buffer itself, or place a charged Battery in an EV machine.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.211: HV Transformer or EV Battery Buffer
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.212: Argon Gas is the third tier of gas used to boost efficiency in the EBF and ABS.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.213: To get Argon Gas you need to run Liquid Air through a Distillation Tower. You also happen to get more Helium Gas and Nitrogen Gas in the process, along with some Oxygen Gas, Carbon Dioxide, and Crushed Ice.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.214: Note you will need at least an HV Input Hatch for the 50,000 mB of Liquid Air input, and also at least an HV Output Hatch for the 35,000 mB of Nitrogen Gas output.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.215: To get Liquid Air you need to run Air through a Vacuum Freezer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.216: To get Air you need to use a Gas Collector in the Overworld. This doesn't require any inputs, just EU and a Programmed Circuit value.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.217: Note that for now it is an optional gas boost, eventually it will be required for the Naquadah-doped Monocrystalline Silicon Boule.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.221: Quantum Eyes are used for HV Field Generators, EV Emitters, EV Sensors, and Qubit CPU Wafers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.222: All except the HV Field Generators being a hard requirement for things soon. Most notably for EV Laser Engravers, EV Circuit Assemblers and the Quantum Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.224: Quantum Stars are used for IV Field Generators, IV Emitters, IV Sensors, and see further use in crafting LuV and ZPM crafting components in the Assembly Line, as well as a further upgrade to Gravi-Stars for later too.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.225: Both Quantum Stars and Gravi-Stars will be hard requirements for quite a few things going forward, most notably the Assembly Line, and many higher tiered crafting components.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.226: Nether Stars can be obtained as normal by killing the Wither, by the Simulation Chamber, or by crafting Nether Star Dust, which does require Rarest Metal Mixture, being part of the Platinum Line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.228: Forged Netherite has an entire GregTech tool line, all being unbreakable.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_hv_age.229: Other recipes that would use standard Netherite Ingots instead use Forged Netherite, and any other items crafted using it that have a durability will be unbreakable when crafted.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.1: The idea of this pack is to get right into GregTech ASAP while making resource generation as easy as possible, GregTech with unlimited ores.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.2_1: Your starting platform and inventory has basically everything you need to jump right into things. When you have the basics down and have Flint and Clay, jump into the
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.3_1: While the main focus is of course GregTech, there are a bunch of utility mods as well that can help a lot with certain things. Check out the
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.3_3: chapter and see a bunch of random things that may help before getting to deep in things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.4: Grab your Diamond Hammer and get to work! You even have an ME Crafting Terminal with a full ME Drive (even 2 Fluid Cells) and a Creative Energy Cell! The Creative Energy Cell can only power AE2.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.5: Almost all "hard mode" recipes have been enabled in the config file, but other than that very few GregTech recipes have been altered. Most other mods have had recipes changed to fit more of a GregTech recipe style and fit the modpack better. AE2 recipes are left as is, use AE2 to your full advantage.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.6: Note that The Nether and The End dimensions are also void worlds but do still spawn structures and the Ender Dragon, although you may never find a need to go to either dimension other than literally collecting Air.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.9: Mine the ore to generate another random ore.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.10: It seems a bit hectic at first but once you get a Raw Ore you want more of, place it in the left GUI slot of the Raw Conversion Generator to generate unlimited amounts of that ore.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.11: This block is basically just to obtain at least 1 of each Raw Ore, then it pretty much becomes useless, unless you happen to use the last of an ore type and need more again.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.12: Keep in mind that there are multiple different ore types that smelt into basic materials like Iron Ingots, Copper Ingots, and Tin Ingots, you can search by tooltips with EMI (prefix of $) or in AE2 (prefix of #) for items by their element name, like Fe for Iron, Cu for Copper, and Sn for Tin. If you double click the EMI search bar, it will highlight any items matching the search in your inventory.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.13: &aYou already have one of these on your platform. You may need to pick it up and place it down to reset it for it to start working, you may not need to.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.16: This will be the main block for generating ores until you get Steel Ingots and can make a better automated version (Simple Ore Generator), which is really not too far away at all.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.17: Insert a Raw Ore of any kind in the left slot of the GUI and the corresponding ore will be generated as a block above the Raw Conversion Generator. The other slots are just basic storage to make swapping ores out easier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.18: The Raw Ore is &nnot consumed&r while generating ores.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.19: Try to remember to always keep at least 1 Raw Ore stored away.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.20: &aYou already have one of these on your platform. You may need to pick it up and place it down to reset it for it to start working, you may not need to.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.23: Does not actually hold Water but can fill Buckets and convert some items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.24: A lot of Clay is going to be needed at the start.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.29: There are other blocks to help with Water generation later on, like the Basic Water Generator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.30: &aYou already have one of these on your platform.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.33: Instead of placing an ore block in the world, this block will generate a random Raw Ore in its 1 slot of inventory. You will need a way to extract the items, like a Hopper or Item Pipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.35: You have a Diamond Hammer in the Item Frame on the starting platform already, &ayou do not need to craft one&r.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.36: Crushing Hammers are used to crush Stone/Cobblestone -> Gravel -> Sand -> Dust. You can also crush Dirt -> random saplings or Plant Fibers (String alternative).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.37: Harvest blocks in world to convert them.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.38: FTB Ultimine works for large groups at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.39: They are also a multi tool, harvesting things that a Pickaxe, Shovel, and Axe would.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.40: GregTech Hammers also process blocks they harvest in the world as they would be in a Forge Hammer, allowing them to obtain Gravel, Sand, and Dust as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.41: Minecraft slows your mining speed down while in creative flight, no clue why as there is absolutely no logic behind that as being in creative mode instantly breaks blocks anyways, but back to the point, there is an &aenchantment&r named &aStable Footing&r that can negate this. It can also be crafted from the Ender IO Enchanter in the early LV age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.45: Does not actually hold Lava but can fill Buckets.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.46: There are other blocks to help with Lava generation later on, like the Basic Lava Generator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.47: &aYou already have one of these on your platform.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.50: Passive mobs can spawn on Grass Blocks with enough light while you are far enough away.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.51: You may also craft a Golden Egg which can be used to create Delightful Dirt, which spawns passive mobs frequently as long as the biome allows it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.52: The Market block also sells (almost) every Spawn Egg, and Spawners are craftable. You can use a Spawn Egg to set a Spawner to that mob type.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.55: This modpack is meant to skip most of the early grind that in normally in skyblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.56: That being said, you start with infinite ore generators with a unique twist.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.57: On the left is the Random Ore Generator which will constantly generate a random ore block above it if there is room, mine the block away and have another random ore generate. This may feel chaotic and too random at first, but once you get a material you want more of, place it in the block on the right, the Raw Conversion Generator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.58: The Raw Conversion Generator will accept 1 Raw Ore of any kind and generate an ore block of that type above it if there is room. &nThe Raw Ore is not consumed.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.59: &6Note you may need to pick them up and place them down again for them to work, sometimes they work on world creation, somtimes they don't.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.60: Being very cheap the idea is to have one set up for each material you need, later having automatic options or just using a Block Breaker.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.61: You have access to every Raw Ore in the modpack and the ability to generate infinite amounts of whichever ore you want.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.62: Ore processing is less important than normal modpacks for obvious reasons, however many required materials are only obtainable as a byproduct so you will need certain processing chains for many different materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.65: Vanilla mechanics for Bone Meal in a Composter. You can easily automate it with a Random Sapling Generator and a couple Hoppers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.72: Home Command - Type /sethome to set a home. Type /home to teleport to that home.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.73: Twerking - Mash sneak to twerk and speed up plant/sapling growth.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.74: FTB Ultimine - Hold the grave key [`] and harvest blocks to harvest up to 64 of that same block as long as they are connected. Just dont mine up your entire base!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.75: Void Garbage - There are actually 2 types of trash cans in your inventory, press [T] to enable a Trash Slot at the bottom of your inventory, or look in the top left of your screen to find the Trash Can, or just take advantage of the ability to hold the throw button [Q] to toss things as far as you can into the void. All options have their own benefits. There is also an Item Trash Can block you can place in the world to pipe items into.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.76: Chunk Claiming - In the top left of your screen when you open your inventory there is a small button that looks like a grid map. This is FTB Chunks, left click a tile to "Claim" the chunk, preventing explosion damage (and more). Shift click a tile to "Force Load" the chunk, meaning it will stay loaded and operating when you are not nearby.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.77_1: Quest Rewards - Quests will reward you with tiered Credits. The Credits can be spent in the
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.77_3: quest chapter. Typically you will be requred to have already held an item to be able to buy the item, so you have to at least have access to what you want to buy first.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.78: Phantoms - Phantoms exist, either build a roof or a Bed, or get a Sleep Charm.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.79: Extreme Sound Muffler - There are a lot of sounds in GregTech, especially in the Steam Age, you can mute any sound you wish by clicking on the volume icon in your inventory to the right of your player model. Note you can also just smack the machine with a GregTech Hammer if you want to only mute a single machine.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.80: Peaceful Mode - It's a valid option, you may be thinking you need a bunch of Ender Pearls, Ender Pearl Dust is craftable in the LV age using ore material. &nEnder Pearl Dust can be converted into Ender Pearls in an Autoclave with Water&r. While Peaceful Mode may take some extra work, it is an option. Ender Pearls, Blaze Powder/Rods, Nether Stars, Dragon's Breath and more can all be crafted, even Apotheosis Gems.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.81: AE2 - Applied Energistics 2 is meant to be as accessible as possible with basically no changed recipes and access before the LV Age. Recipes have only been added to fit a skyblock modpack and &nchannels have been disabled&r to allow easier automation for the mass amount of machines you will have. Quite a few addon mods for AE2 are present as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.84: The Nether is a void dimension as well but it still has structures.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.85: Build a portal as normal with Obsidian or craft a Nether Painting. If using Paintings for travel, remember to bring an Overworld Painting with you to get back as they do not create a return. You can also just use /home if you set your home at your base with /sethome.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.86: The only reason you will probably need to go here is for Nether Air.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.87: You have to &njump&r into the Painting.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.90: GregTech Item Pipes and Fluid Pipes can be less ideal to work with in certain situations, due to this quite a few logistical mods like Modular Routers, LaserIO, XNet, and Conduits from EnderIO have been added for more transfer options.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.91: There's nothing wrong with GregTech logistical options, but they are not very compact and sometimes a different method can be much better.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.95: Quests are mostly to show progression and point some things out that might be helpful. They are in no way required, you could ignore them completely and just look through EMI and be fine.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.96_1: Quests will reward you with tiered Credits. The Credits can be spent in the
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.96_3: quest chapter. Typically you will be requred to have already held an item to be able to buy the item, so you have to at least have access to what you want to buy first. You can also craft lower tier Credits into higher tier Credits, and higher tier Credits into lower tier Credits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.97: Quest chapters may look a bit web like sometimes, but a lot of effort goes in to making sure dependency lines do not cross through other quests as this tends to look confusing and misleading. Lines will cross through other lines, but not through other quests, unless there was physically no other option.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.98: Quests with &2sharp square&r icons are things &2required for progression&r, &3rounded square&r icons are &3optional&r and just something being pointed out, &6gear&r icons are just &6informational&r reading/checkbox quests, and &dhexagon/octagon&r icons are often a &dmilestone&r of some kind.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.99: "Entry Point" quests will be slightly larger than quests that are locked behind other quests, but not as large as milestone quests. This is just to get a better visual on where to start in a quest chapter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.100: Any quest for a fluid will show the filled fluid Bucket, however the quest task is marked as optional, and there is also a checkbox task. This is just so you can easily see the recipe for the fluid, and the checkbox task is you saying you have obtained the fluid. This was a better route than requiring holding the filled fluid Bucket and still giving the option to open EMI from the quest.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.101: Quests are being worked on constantly, quests and quest chapters will be added, updated, or removed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.102: Quests are mostly finished up to the UV age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.104: WIP but a ton of content to UV!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.106: Harvest Cobblestone (or Stone) with a Crushing Hammer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.108: You already have an active Cobble Gen on your platform if you haven't found it yet.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.110: Harvest Gravel with a Crushing Hammer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.113: Use the Dust block on a Primitive Water Condenser to create Clay.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.114: You &ocan&r use the stone dust variants you get from mining ores on a Primitive Water Condenser to create Clay Balls, but you may want to save some of those dusts, especially the Stone Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.115: You may find it easier to just make the Clay block first then turn those into Clay Balls from there with whatever method.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.116: You can also craft Clay with a GregTech Hammer, use the Cutting Board from Farmer's Delight, or just mine the Clay normally to obtain Clay Balls.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.117: Clay is basically all you need to properly start the Steam Age, and obviously a Furnace and some basic ores.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.119: Harvest Sand with a Crushing Hammer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.120: Use on the Primitive Water Condenser to create Clay.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.122: Harvest Dirt with a Crushing Hammer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.123: You have a chance to get a random sapling or Plant Fibers, which can be used as and also turned into String.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.124: You already have an active Dirt Gen on your platform if you haven't found it yet.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.126: Phantoms are annoying, sleep to keep them away for a few more days. You can also just build a roof and they won't bother you. They will only spawn if your head can see the sky.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.127: Note that White Wool can be crafted from normal String, and Lime Wool can be crafted directly from Plant Fibers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.128: You can also craft a Sleep Charm which gives you immunity to Insomnia, which is what makes Phantoms spawn. It also allows you to sleep much faster.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.131: Harvest Gravel with something that is &6not the Crushing Hammer&r for a chance of obtaining Flint.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.132: Use FTB Ultimine to harvest a stack at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.133: Once you can make Stone in a Furnace you can craft a Mortar to obtain Flint much easier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.135: Pretty simple blocks, will generate 1 random sapling or seed per second and store it in its internal inventory. Use a Hopper or any other method to automate them.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.136: All saplings and seeds can be purchased from the Market block as well but this could be accessed a bit earlier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.137: If you need seeds look into the Composter quest for Bone Meal and use the Bone Meal on a Grass Block, or buy them from the Market block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.140: Even though the Raw Conversion Generator will generate a specific ore type, it still cycles randomly through the stone variant types of that ore, that can be annoying when trying to mine with a Pickaxe or Shovel as the required tool type changes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.141: That's where this block comes in, it will look below itself and if there is an ore block below it, it will generate that exact same ore block above itself. Meaning, if you have your Netherrack Diamond Ore below it, it will generate a Netherrack Diamond Ore above itself every time you mine it away.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.142: A decent early strategy for mining is to use these and make a 3x3 of different ores you want to mine in the same stone type variant. Then you can just mine from above with a Mining Hammer and mine 9 different ore types at once and never be interrupted by Sand or Gravel Ores.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.144: Just a faster version of the Simple Ore Generator, works at twice the speed, and it's purple this time.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.146: The Market allows you to buy most seeds, saplings, crops, random world gen stuff, and even Spawn Eggs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.147: You can either Bone Meal the Grass Blocks and maybe get a Poppy, or turn Redstone Dust into Red Dye using a Mortar if needed for the recipe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.148: Wool can be made from Plant Fiber early on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.150: Most standard Minecraft recipes are altered by GregTech, making them a bit more involved, some more than others.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.151: The Furnace is probably the first look at that, not much different, but does require some Flint to craft.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.153: This is just your very basic start to sky block mechanics to get the basics like Gravel, Sand, Clay, and such.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.156: If you are familiar with sky blocks, you probably are not familiar with this.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.157: There is no sifting, sieving, crushing Gravel into ore chunks, none of that.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.158: The blocks below are the basic ore generation blocks and their upgraded versions.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.159: Ore generation in this pack is essentially infinite, easily obtainable, and not much work required at all. Obtaining ores is not supposed to be an issue here, it's more about what you do with them once you have them.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.160: While you do start off mining ore blocks that generate in the world, once you have Steel Ingots everything is easily automated with the Simple Ore Generator block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.164: Both the Raw Conversion Generator and the Random Ore Generator should have a Coal Ore above them. You start with Coal Ores so you can instantly start smelting things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.165: Mining the Coal Ore above the Raw Conversion Generator will make more Coal Ore spawn, mining the Coal Ore from above the Random Ore Generator will make another random ore spawn.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.166: You can use the Advanced Item Collector given from the reward to help pickup all the ores you mine. If you place it with the base connedted to an inventory it will automatically put anything it picks up into the inventory.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.169_1: If you are new to GregTech there is a lot to learn. The quests through the earlier stages will usually include quite a bit of information but you may want to check out the
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.169_3: informational quest chapter which goes over some basics in detail.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.170: Click the underlined words above to go directly to that quest chapter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.173: Place under certain blocks to generate that block type as an item in its internal inventory at a rate of 1 per second.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.174: Blocks that can be made infinite are tagged with the block tag "infinite_blocks:infinite_blocks". You can search EMI for #infinite_blocks and see the blocks available.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.175: The Rock Breaker from GregTech can also produce anything that the Infinite Block Generator can produce, and faster, allowing machine overclocking to reduce the duration.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.180: - Blocks in the concretes tag (not GregTech).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_intro.187: &aTip: You can easily obtain Clay Dust with this.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.2: Rhodium Plated Palladium is the main material for the LuV Age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.3: You can use either a Mixer or the ABS as it is an alloy.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.5: Used to craft IV Energy Hatches, IV Dynamo Hatches, and opens up access to the Advanced Generators mod if you wish to go that route.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.7: Iridium will see quite a bit of uses going forward, most notably for the EV Circuit Assembler, Insane Voltage Coil, and Power Substation, but also crafting components, Pipes, and Turbine Rotor as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.8: Will also later be required for Osmiridium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.10: Used in multiblock generators to handle an IV rating EU output.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.13: Typically used in making IV energy related items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.15: Next tier of PIC Wafers, for now used to make HPIC Chips, later on used to make UHPIC Wafers as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.17: Used in the process to make HPIC Wafers/Chips, and eventually LuV Superconductor Wires.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.18: Later on with the Naquadah Line you will gain access to another route for Indium Dust, this process could be replaced fully by that.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.19: Leads to HPIC materials and LuV Superconductors!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.20: Used for making the HPIC Wafers, Advanced SMD Diodes, and some other higher tier Wafers down the road.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.21: Upgrading the Wafers and SMD Diodes!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.22: Some people dislike power generation in the higher ages of GregTech. Advanced Generators was added as an alternative power source for the IV age and up. If you want, you can now generate FE using Advanced Generators. You can convert it into EU as normal. You can place an Energy Converter directly touching the Flux Generator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.24: These generators can scale quite high, holding up to 50 Turbines per generator. The highest tier Turbines are not available until the LuV age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.25: &aDefault generation rates for Turbines have been buffed. All fuel types from GregTech can be used in a Gas Turbine. GregTech Steam and Advanced Generators Steam are interchangable.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.26: GregTech will always be a better energy solution in the long run but this is an option for now. The highest tier Turbine is gated behind Naquadah Alloy.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.29: This is not a multiblock Assembler, however it is similar. The Assembly Line is crucial to further progression as this is where most higher tier crafting components are made.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.30: Almost all recipes in the Assembly Line require Liquid Soldering Alloy, it's rather easy to make, but is required for most recipes so you'll always need some on hand.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.32: The setup of this multiblock is kind of similar to the setup of a Distillation Tower. You need to extend the multiblock for however many inputs the recipe has.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.33: &6Input Buses must be ULV.&r If the recipe has 8 input materials, it will need 8 &3Input Buses&r, and be in the &3bottom center line of the multiblock&r. The &5Output Bus&r is always required to be the &5last one in the chain after the Input Buses&r, so if you have 8 inputs, the Assembly Line will be 9 blocks wide, the last being for the Output Bus.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.34: &2Input Hatches&r, and can replace any of the Solid Machine Casings on the &2bottom level that are not in the center line&r, and &eEnergy Hatches&r can replace any of the Solid Machine Casings on the &etop level&r.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.35: The Input Buses must be in the proper order they appear in the recipe, and must have the first input being in the Input Bus closest to the controller.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.37: Most (almost all) recipes require a Data Stick, Data Orb, or Data Module to be programmed in order to work. A Scanner is required in order to program a Data Stick. The Data Orb and Data Module require the Research Station.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.38: Recipes involving Data items can look confusing at first. For example, EMI shows a Data Stick + ZPM Input Bus will craft an Object Holder, this is not quite true. What it actually does is program the Data Stick to be set to an Object Holder, that programmed Data Stick is then used in the Assembly Line as basically a guide/blueprint type item to state what will be crafted, the actual Object Holder.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.39: &n&aThe Data item is not consumed in the crafting process.&r&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.42: A Ruthenium Iridium alloy, a requirement for the Assembly Line and used in some crafting components later on as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.43: Ruridit Dust requires an IV Mixer, however Molten Ruridit only requires an EV ABS with RTM Alloy Coils.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.45: A central energy storage multiblock. The tier of the Dynamo Hatch you use determines the energy output rate. You can have multiple Dynamo Hatches, allowing different rates of energy to be extracted from different Dynamo Hatches. You can even have multiple different voltages of Dynamo Hatches to allow extracting different voltages from different Dynamo Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.46: 64A Substation Energy and Dynamo Hatches are special Energy and Dynamo Hatches for the Power Substation, allowing up to 64 amps to travel in or out of a single Hatch. They are available in EV to UHV.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.47: A minimum of 14 Palladium Substation Casings are required, leaving room for many Energy and Dynamo Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.48: Allows up to 18 layers of Capacitors, the Capacitors do not need the be the same tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.49: Loses energy equal to 1% of total capacity every 24 hours. Capped at 100k EU/t passive loss per Capacitor Block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.52: HSS-G sees quite a few uses, most notably the HSS-G Coils, Advanced SMD Transistors, IV Rotor Holder, Turbine Rotor, and the first ZPM Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.53: HSS-G Dust is also used to make HSS-E and HSS-S materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.58: The IV Superconductor, has a loss of 0 EU per block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.59: Also required for IV Field Generators which will start becoming required for progression soon.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.61: As normal, the only use it has is for Superconductors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.62: You can either use an IV Mixer or an EV ABS, but you would need HSS-G Coils if using the ABS.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.64: In order to get Samarium Dust you need the Small Pile of Samarium Dust obtained from Rare Earth in a Centrifuge.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.65: Used to make IV Superconductors, and has more uses for LuV, ZPM, and UV crafting components.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.66: Samarium is the final tier of Magnetic Rods which will be used from LuV through UV, and they require an IV Polarizer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.69: Right click on a Block of Iridium while holding any item that uses durability in your main hand to fully repair the item and make the item unbreakable while consuming the Block of Iridium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.71: The root source of Indium Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.77: This is the start to the Nanoprocessor Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.78: The whole Nanoprocessor Circuit line requires a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.79: This is the third HV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.80: Next tier of CPU Chips, typically used in making Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.82: Liquid Epoxy is used the make the Epoxy Printed Circuit Board, used in an EV Circuit Assembler or higher to make the Nanoprocessor Circuit line and Data Orbs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.83: While you can make the Epoxy Printed Circuit Boards much earlier, they see no use until now.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.86: Next tier of CPU Wafers, for now used to make Nano CPU Chips, later on used to make Qubit Wafers as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.88: This is the second EV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.89: This is the second IV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.90: The third tier of Wafer material.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.91: Cuts into 64 Naquadah-doped Wafers at a time and better output ratios for Laser Engraving than the second tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.93: When using the Advanced SMD components to make Circuits you need far less than the standard versions. The recipes using Advanced SMD components are also faster than the standard ones.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.94: While still an optional upgrade, later they will be required for higher tier Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.97: While some multiblocks have Large in the name, there is a specific set of multiblocks referred to as the "Large Series".
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.98: These multiblocks have a unique trait to them as they all allow a Parallel Hatch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.99: Parallel hatches allow multiple recipes to run at once, taking the same normal duration as a single recipe, but scaling the input/output quantities and the EU/t by the parallel amount.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.100: For this reason most single block machines will no longer appear in quests, as you can and should be using the Large Series multiblocks instead.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.101: &6Note that both the Large Assembling Factory and Large Circuit Assembly Facility only accept 1 Energy Hatch, not allowing recipe tier skips.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.102_3: quest in the multiblock overview chapter for a list of the Large Series multiblocks available.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.105: The first available Parallel Hatch, can allow up to 4 recipes to run at the same time. Later tiers of Parallel Hatches allow 16, 64, and 256 recipes at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.106: When running parallel recipes, the input, output, and EU/t is scaled by the parallel amount. Because of the EU/t scaling you will generally require a multi amp Energy Hatch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.107: Not all multiblocks can accept a Parralel Hatch, but if the multiblock controller's tooltip says it can parallelize with Parallel Control Hatches, they can accept one. The EMI multiblock preview will also state if they can accept one.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.108: Typically all of the "Large Series" multiblocks can accept one, and some others.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.110: The Extreme Combustion Engine is an upgrade to the Large Combustion Engine. It requires both a fuel source as normal, and also a small amount of Lubricant (1000 mB an hour).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.112: If you also provide 80 mB of &6Liquid Oxygen&r (not Oxygen Gas) per second it will produce 32,768 EU/t (4A of IV), at the cost of twice the fuel consumption.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.113: Uses 2 times the fuel to produce 4 times the EU/t when Oxygen boosted.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.114: &aOxygen Boosting requires at least a 4A or 16A IV Dynamo Hatch or an LuV Dynamo Hatch as a standard IV Dynamo Hatch only has 2A and cannot accept that much EU/t.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.115: &6The 16A Dynamo Hatches have no effect with the Combustion Engines and they show improper information when doing so.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.118: Works the same as the basic single block Simple Ore Generators, but generates a stack at a time of end ore variants very quickly.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.119: Often not needed, unless you require thousands of something for large scale crafts and don't have a large stock.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.122: Used to process recipes with an IV requirement.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.123: Can and should be used to upgrade the the Large Series version when possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.125: Part of the Large Series multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.126: Allows a Parallel Hatch, and can do a sub tick overclock if recipes become fast enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.127: While it can only accept 1 Energy Hatch, you can still use multi amp Energy Hatches in order to provide enough EU to handle the parallel recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.128: The ABS alloy required is Stellite-100.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.129: No Muffler Hatch is required, meaning it can be used in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.130: Note that the single block Assemblers will still often be required, as typically to make the next tier of Energy Hatch you need the next tier Assembler, and with no tier boosting for the Large Assembling Factory, you still need the single block version sometimes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.133: Naquadah has a lot of uses, but not typically in the base form. It is mostly used in further alloys or chemical chains. However, it is required for the Naquadah-doped Monocrystalline Silicon Boule and of course the Naquadah Coils.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.134: Naquadah will be part of the ZPM ingot, but it will be Naquadah Alloy, and there is also Naquadria later on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.135: To get Naquadah Dust you need to do some ore processing steps, ideally you want to get some of the Enriched Naquadah Dust as well for later on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.136: Note to cool down the Hot Naquadah Ingots in the Vacuum Freezer, you need &aLiquid Helium&r, &6not Helium Gas&r. You will also get half of the Liquid Helium used back as Helium Gas.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.137: You can make Liquid Helium by running Helium Gas through a Vacuum Freezer which is a 1:1 ratio.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.139: Part of the Large Series multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.140: Allows a Parallel Hatch, and can do a sub tick overclock if recipes become fast enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.141: The ABS alloys required are Hastelloy X, and Maraging Steel 300.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.142: No Muffler Hatch is required, meaning it can be used in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.145: Used to process recipes with an IV requirement.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.146: Can and should be used to upgrade the the Large Series version when possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.148: A basic alloy of 1 Osmium and 3 Iridium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.149: Used for quite a bit going forward, including Naquadah Alloy and ZPM crafting components.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.150: While it does seem like you require an LuV Mixer, you can tier skip with the ABS with 2 IV Energy Hatches to get an LuV rating in the ABS instead.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.152: Another upgrade to the Energy Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.154: The IV Field Generator is the first Field Generator to actually be required for progression, being used in the Fusion Reactor MK I controller, the Fusion Coil Block, and used to make further Field Generators, again required for more things as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.156: Requires an EV Cutter in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.157: Not only goes the Boule cut into more Raw Wafers, but the Laser Engraver step also produces more Engraved Wafers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.158: Requires an EV Laser Engraver in a Cleanroom to process into Engraved Wafers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.159: The only new unique Chip to be that can be made is the ASoC Chip, which will be required for making the Nanoprocessor and Quantum Processor Circuit lines.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.161: Requires an EV Laser Engraver and a Purple or Amethyst Lens in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.163: Used for making the Nanoprocessor and Quantum Processor Circuit lines cheaper and faster than the standard recipes, replacing all the SMD components with just the ASoC Chip instead.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.165: Used to process recipes with an IV requirement.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.166: Can and should be used to upgrade the the Large Series version when possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.168: Part of the Large Series multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.169: Works as a Cutter and a Lathe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.170: Allows a Parallel Hatch, and can do a sub tick overclock if recipes become fast enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.171: The ABS alloy required is Hastelloy C-276.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.172: No Muffler Hatch is required, meaning it can be used in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.175: Part of the Large Series multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.176: Allows a Parallel Hatch, and follows the same logic for Coils as the standard Pyrolyse Oven.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.177: The ABS alloy required is Titanosteel Alloy.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.180: Part of the Large Series multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.181: Works as a Distillation Tower and a Distillery. If using as a Distillation Tower it still scales vertically depending on the recipe outputs as normal.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.182: Allows a Parallel Hatch, and can do a sub tick overclock if recipes become fast enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.183: The ABS alloy required is Watertight Steel.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.184: No Muffler Hatch is required, meaning it can be used in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.189: LuV Cables and up start to require Polyphenylene Sulfide Sheets.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.190: Polyphenylene Sulfide isn't too much of a process actually. Chances are you already have access to all the base materials. Benzene is the only non standard material at this point.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.194: An alloy of HSS-G, Osmium, and Iridium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.195: HSS-S is what all of the LuV crafting components are made of, like Robot Arms, Conveyors, and so on, and you typically need quite a lot.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.196: HSS-S Dust requires an IV Mixer, however Molten HSS-S only requires an EV ABS with HSS-G Coils.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.198: Part of the Large Series multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.199: Allows a Parallel Hatch, and can do a sub tick overclock if recipes become fast enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.200: While it can only accept 1 Energy Hatch, you can still use multi amp Energy Hatches in order to provide enough EU to handle the parallel recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.201: The ABS alloy required is Stellite-100.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.202: No Muffler Hatch is required, meaning it can be used in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.204: Typically the Circuit Assembler tends to kind of be part of the next age but this is worth pointing out sooner than later.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.205: The IV Circuit Assembler is technically the last Circuit Assembler you need to make, as you can make the Large Circuit Assembling Facility multiblock with it, and it can also be used in a Cleanroom too.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.206: Swapping to the Large Series multiblock has obvious benefits, as well as no longer needing the single block upgrades, just upgrade the Energy Hatch, however do note that it only accept 1 Energy Hatch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.207: The last Circuit Assembler you'll need!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.208: The final tier of Magnetic Rods.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.209: Requires an IV rating, at this point you can either use the IV single block version, the Semi Perfect Electromagnet, or the Large Electromagnet.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.210: You may not want the single block version though, may as well go for one of the multiblocks at this point.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.212: Osmium Ingots require an LuV EBF so you will need to use 2 IV Energy Hatches to start.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.214: Used to process recipes with an IV requirement.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.215: Can and should be used to upgrade the the Large Series version when possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.217: Part of the Large Series multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.218: Allows a Parallel Hatch, and can do a sub tick overclock if recipes become fast enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.219: No ABS alloy is required, instead the casings are made from HSLA Steel.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.220: No Muffler Hatch is required, meaning it can be used in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.223: The Simulation Arena is a mob farm simulation multiblock.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.224: It uses a Spawn Egg as a non consumable input to state which mob to simulate, and a Simulation Chip as a consumable input per iteration, as well as some Formic Acid.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.225: Spawn Eggs can be purchased from the Market block, as well as Wither Spawn Eggs which for whatever reason cannot be seen in EMI.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.226: If the mob has multiple drops that can be obtained, the Programmed Circuit value of 10 will act as a random chance for outputs from the pool of items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.227: You can also select which drop to target by using a specific Programmed Circuit value. This does take 3 times longer than the random output.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.228: Some mobs give a fluid output as well, like Blazes giving Liquid Blaze, Nether mobs giving Nether Air, End mobs giving Ender Air, Warden giving Fluid XP, and some others. If a fluid output is present it will always be produced, it does not follow chanced outputs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.229: The Coils used act like they do in the Cracker Unit, reducing EU cost depending on the Coil tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.231: &aA great way to get Nether Stars.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.233: The Data Bank can be used to store many Data Sticks, Data Orbs, and Data Modules as it allows multiple Data Access Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.234: It requires transmitting the data through Optical Fiber Cables.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.235: Optical Fiber Cables can only have a single point to point connection from Optical Data Transmission Hatch to Optical Data Reception Hatch. Because of this if you are sending data to more than 1 Assembly Line, you will require more than 1 Optical Data Transmission Hatch and have a separate Optical Fiber Cable line to and from each Transmission and Reception Hatch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.236: The Data Access Hatch required for the Assembly Line can be replaced with an Optical Data Reception Hatch, allowing it to access the Data Sticks, Data Orbs, or Data Modules required directly from the Data Bank.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.237: Any of the Computer Casings except the ones in the interior can be replaced with Data Access Hatches, Optical Data Transmission Hatches, and Optical Data Reception Hatches. The minimum required Computer Casings is only 3, but this does not include the 3 Computer Casings in the interior.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.238: Data Banks can also be chained together using an Optical Data Transmission Hatch from 1 Data Bank into an Optical Data Reception Hatch on another Data Bank, allowing the second Data Bank to access all the data from the first Data Bank.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_iv_age.239: &6Data Modules can only be inserted into an active Data Bank.&r They can still be inserted into whatever type of Data Access Hatch you have on the Data Bank, but they cannot be inserted into the Data Access Hatch on a Assembly Line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.1: LaserIO is all about sending items, fluids, FE, and redstone signals through lasers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.2: The main block of the mod is the Laser Node. You will have 1 of these every time you want to insert or extract something.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.3: You need to insert Cards into the Laser Node in order for it to function. Change the Card to insert or extract mode by right clicking with or on the Card and opening the GUI. This is where you can also set Filters and Overclockers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.4: Use a Laser Wrench to connect Laser Nodes together and if you need to travel more than 8 blocks, use Laser Connectors to travel longer distances.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.5: Since Cards do not stack, you can place them in the Card Holder to keep all your Cards, Filters, and Overclockers in 1 container.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.6: Filters can be used in a few ways to decide what goes where, and Overclockers can be used to upgrade Cards and Laser Nodes to function faster.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.9: A Laser Node is used to interact with things by using Cards. Insert Cards to determine what you want it to do. Can hold up to 9 Cards per face.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.10: Right clicking on a face of a Laser Node with a Card in your hand will insert the Card into that face.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.11: Link 2 Laser Nodes together with a Laser Wrench. Has a maximum linking range of 8 blocks, farther lengths can be achieved by using Laser Connectors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.13: - Chest with a Laser Node beside it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.14: - In the Laser Node on the face touching the Chest insert an Item Card.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.15: - Right click on the Item Card to Open the GUI.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.16: - Set this Item Card to Extract.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.17: - Another Chest within 8 blocks with a Laser Node beside it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.18: - Sneak right click with a Laser Wrench on the first Laser Node, right click on the second Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.19: - In the second Laser Node on the face touching the Chest insert an Item Card.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.20: - By default all Cards are set to Insert mode so you shouldn't have to change it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.21: - Now items in the first Chest will be sent to the second Chest.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.22: This works the same for items, fluids, FE, and redstone signals.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.23: If you need to go farther distances, look into the Laser Connectors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.24: For the glowing issue with shaders, turn off bloom in shaders. "Options..." -> "Video Settings..." -> "Shader Packs..." -> "Shader Pack Settings..." -> "Camera" -> "Bloom": Off.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.27: A Laser Node can only connect to another Laser Node or Laser Connector in an 8 block range. If you need to go farther than 8 blocks, you will need to use a Laser Connector as a relay to another Laser Connector or Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.28: - Connect a Laser Node to a Laser Relay.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.29: - Connect the Laser Relay to another Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.30: - Both Laser Nodes will now interact with each other.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.31: Advanced Laser Connectors go much farther distances.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.33: Instead of making an actual link, they send and receive contents through a small void portal, allowing infinite range and cross dimensional distances.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.35: Used to link together Laser Nodes and/or Laser Connectors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.36: Sneak right click on a block to select that block. Right click on another block to connect to that block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.38: Stores and stacks Cards, Overclockers, and Filters.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.39: Contents can be accessed while using Laser Nodes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.41: Used to copy and paste the settings of Cards from 1 Card to another.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.42: - Open a Laser Node containing cards.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.43: - Pick up the Card Cloner with your mouse.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.44: - Hover over the Card you wish to copy and left click it with the Card Cloner.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.45: - Hover over the Card you witsh to paste to and right click it with the Card Cloner.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.47: Used to transfer items. Open the GUI by right clicking while holding it or while hovering over it with your mouse while in a Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.48: You can change the insert/extract mode and insert Filters and Overclockers, as well as change the transfer rate and amounts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.50: Used to transfer fluids. Open the GUI by right clicking while holding it or while hovering over it with your mouse while in a Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.51: You can change the insert/extract mode and insert Filters and Overclockers, as well as change the transfer rate and amounts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.53: Used to transfer FE (not EU!). Open the GUI by right clicking while holding it or while hovering over it with your mouse while in a Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.54: You can change the insert/extract mode and insert Filters and Overclockers, as well as change the transfer rate and amounts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.56: Used to transfer redstone signals. Open the GUI by right clicking while holding it or while hovering over it with your mouse while in a Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.57: You can change the insert/extract mode and signal strength.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.59: Insert into a Card to increase transfer rates and amounts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.60: A maximum of 4 can be applied to a Card.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.61: Transfer speeds can be very fast with a few of these, being much faster than any GregTech transfer option in the early to mid game.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.63: Insert into a Laser Node. Without Node Overclockers a Laser Node will only work with 1 Card at a time, insert Node Overclockers to increase that number to a maximum to 9 (1 for each Card).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.64: A maximum of 8 can be applied to a Laser Node.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.66: A basic filter that allows you to choose which items or fluids pass through.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.68: Used to specify certain amounts of items/fluids that enter the attached inventory.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.69: Useful for keeping 1 stack each of certain items stocked inside a machine, like an Alloy Furnace.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.71: Place an item in the GUI (or drag from REI) and you will be shown a list of tags that item has. Select the tag you want to be allowed through the Tag Filter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.72: For an example, you can place a Hot Ingot of any kind in the GUI slot and select forge:hot_ingots to allow all Hot Ingots.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.74: Place an item in the Mod Filter to select that entire mod of contents. Only items or fluids from that mod will be allowed to pass.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.76: Works similar to the Tag Filter but for NBT values instead.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.77: Common NBT value types are durability, enchantments, potion types, and more.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.79: While not required to craft the Cards, Overclockers, and Filters from LaserIO, they can craft them much more effeciently.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.80: If crafting Cards in bulk, have the Card Assembler auto output into something with a large inventory as unfortunately the Cards do not stack.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_laserio.81: The higher tier machines will just run faster, they will not effect recipes other than duration and EU/t.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.2: Naquadah Alloy is the main material for the ZPM Age.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.6: Also used in a couple more alloys in the UV age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.11: The LuV Superconductor, has a loss of 0 EU per block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.12: Also used in making the Superconducting Coil Block, required for the Fusion Reactor and Active Transformer multiblocks.
