sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.17: Can be made using either LuV, ZPM, or UV 2x Superconductors, each higher tier needing less.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.20: This is the second LuV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.21: Used in an EV Circuit Assembler or higher to make Lapotronic Energy Orbs, or an IV Circuit Assembler or higher to make the Quantum Processor Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.22: While you can make the Fiber-Reinforced Printed Circuit Boards much earlier, they see no use until now except for the Lapotronic Energy Orbs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.24: This is the third IV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.25: The final tier of CPU Wafers, used to make Qubit CPU Chips.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.26: Has 2 options for recipes, either using Quantum Eyes and Liquid Gallium Arsenide, or Indium Gallium Phosphide Dust and Radon Gas. Either are viable, the Quantum Eye recipe is a bit faster though.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.28: The final tier of CPU Chips, used in making the Quantum Processor Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.30: The start to the Quantum Processor Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.31: This is the third EV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.32: Can combine any number of Energy Inputs into any number of Energy Outputs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.33: The Active Transformer is effectively all tiers of transformers at once. Unlike a normal Transformer, you don't need to change voltages from one to another, instead you can feed whatever voltages you want into the Active Transformer via Energy Hatches, and extract whatever voltage you want out via Dynamo Hatches. Of course to do so you need to have the proper Energy and Dynamo Hatches setup.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.37: The fifth and final PIC Chip.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.38: Typically used in making LuV, ZPM, and UV energy related items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.39: This is probably the first requirement for a Cutter that has an LuV rating, which can either be the LuV Cutter or the Large Cutting Saw with 2 IV Energy Hatches or an LuV Energy Hatch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.40: The Semi Perfect Cutting Saw cannot be used as the recipe needs a Cleanroom and it has a Muffler Hatch, but the Large Cutting Saw does not and can be used in a Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.42: The final tier of PIC Wafers, used to make UHPIC Chips.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.44: Used to process recipes with an LuV requirement.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.45: You are going to need to have the Assembly Line working to make all of the LuV crafting components like Electric Motors and Robots Arms and such.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.47: Another upgrade to the Energy Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.49: The LuV Dual Hatches are the first ones available, acting as both an Input/Output Bus and Hatch at the same time. This can make AE2 Patterns much simpler with multiblocks that require both items and fluids, skipping the need for any kind of subnet or buffer between the Pattern Provider and the multiblock inputs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.51: Nothing too special about the LuV Input Bus compared to other versions other than the inventory size, but used to make the LuV Dual Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.52: This may be your first hard requirement for Polybenzimidazole.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.54: Nothing too special about the LuV Input Hatch compared to other versions other than the tank size, but used to make the LuV Dual Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.55: This may be your first hard requirement for Polybenzimidazole.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.57: The Large Plasma Turbines actually have a base EU generation of an EV rating instead of the normal LV being scaled up, this doesn't really change much though, just be aware when looking at the fuel usage recipes in EMI.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.58: You will always get a gas or fluid as an output depending on the plasma fuel type you use.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.59: Helium Plasma is the worst plasma fuel type, burning 1 mB over 2 seconds @ 1920 EU/t.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.60: Americium Plasma is the best plasma fuel type, burning 1 mB over 16 seconds @ 1920 EU/t.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.62: Uses 2 fluid inputs and a large amount of energy, creating fusion materials in the process. Quite a few fusion materials will be required going forward, some requiring a higher tier Fusion Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.63: There is a lot to read here as Fusion Reactors tend to behave rather unique compared to other multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.64: See the different pages of this quest for information split by category.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.66: Quite a few materials can be made much easier with a Fusion Reactor, look through the recipes and see the fluids it can make that you have been using a lot of through progression and see if it feels more viable to switch to a Fusion Reactor. Just keep the startup EU cost in mind, you don't really want it stopping and starting constantly.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.67: Requires a significant startup EU cost and more EU/t to keep the process going. The EU/t used to run after it has been started is nowhere near the EU cost to start it so it is best to keep it running. The startup EU cost is based on the internal "Heat" level seen in the GUI. When a recipe pauses or stops, the heat starts to drop. When the Fusion Reactor starts up again, the startup EU cost is relative to how much heat is required to get back to full. So with a heat of 0, it needs the full startup EU cost, if the heat was 75% of full, it needs 25% of the startup EU cost.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.68: For some things you will want to use Machine Controller Covers and some kind of system for reading storage amounts to make it so the Fusion Reactor doesn't start and stop too often. You can use ME Threshold Level Emitters to send redstone signals based on storage values, or ME Threshold Export Busses to only export the inputs when there is between a certain amount available to help prevent on/off flickering. GregTech does have Covers for this too, but the AE2 methods are a bit easier to manage and use.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.70: &aCan only accept LuV, ZPM, and UV Energy Hatches.&r &6You do NOT need to power every Energy Hatch.&r Providing energy to any Energy Hatch will fill the buffer of the Fusion Reactor and the EU/t required to run recipes can always be handled by just 1 or 2 Energy Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.71: For every Energy Hatch it has, the EU buffer increases by 10M EU, to a max of 160M EU. This is the value shown in the actual Fusion Reactor controller block. So 16 Energy Hatches will get to the maximum buffer size. Some recipes require a larger buffer, but you may as well just start with the maximum since the Energy Hatches are cheaper than the Fusion Machine Casings anyways.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.72: &aThe Input and Output Hatches can be any tier.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.73: Filter the unused Output Hatches with something like Water (or anything really) to force the output to a specific Output Hatch as you generally don't need all the Output Hatches but they are still viable to build the structure with to save a ton on Fusion Machine Casings.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.74: You can substitute some of the Fusion Machine Casings for Fusion Glass, but not all of them. You can have &aup to 31 Fusion Glass&r in place of Fusion Machine Casings. Note there is &6certain spots that the Fusion Glass is allowed&r, not just in place of any Fusion Machine Casings.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.75: &aIf using all 16 Input Hatches, Output Hatches, and Energy Hatches, and all 31 Fusion Glass, you need 48 Fusion Machine Casings.&r This is the same for all Fusion Reactor tiers. The only difference in structure for the tiers are the Fusion Machine Casings and the minimum Energy Hatch tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.76: You can stack them on top of each other for wall sharing purposes and use the top layer of a Fusion Reactor as the bottom layer of the next Fusion Reactor, saving a ton of resources on Fusion Machine Casings.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.77: &aWhen wall sharing by stacking, the next Fusion Reactor above only needs 24 (not 48) Fusion Machine Casings, 31 Fusion Glass, 8 (not 16) Input Hatches, 16 output Hatches, and 16 Energy Hatches.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.79: &6To run a Fusion Reactor recipe at an overclocked rate, you need to run it in a higher tier Fusion Reactor. Just upgrading the Energy Hatches does not work like normal.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.80: For Fusion Reactors they have set tiers, being: MK I = LuV, MK II = ZPM, MK III = UV.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.81: Overclocking a Fusion Reactor recipe cuts the duration in half while doubling the EU/t. So the total EU stays the same like a perfect overclock, but it only does duration/2 and EU/t*2 instead of duration/4 and EU/t*4.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.83_3: quest chapter for a detailed view of all fusion recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.86: Europium starts as Liquid Europium obtained using the MK I Fusion Reactor with Liquid Neodymium and Hydrogen Gas.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.87: Europium has many uses, mostly in the form of Fine Europium Wire and different sized Cables.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.91: Helium Plasma is the first plasma fuel type you have access to with the MK I Fusion Reactor, also it is not actually made using Helium at all. It is made from Deuterium Gas and Tritium Gas.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.92: Deuterium Gas can come from Hydrogen Gas or Ender Air in a Centrifuge, or &6Liquid&r Ender Air a Distillation Tower.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.93: Tritium Gas can come from Deuterium Gas in a Centrifuge or &6Liquid&r Ender Air in a Distillation Tower.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.94: While you don't require the Distillation Tower route, you may want to as it is also the only way to obtain Xenon and Krypton, and gives quite a bit of extra byproducts as well. Just make sure your Output Hatches are large enough for the large quantities of outputs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.100: Required for the Fusion Reactor MK II, some HPCA parts, the Research Station, and the ZPM Field Generator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.102: Can perform up to 16 recipes at once, as long as you have the EU to support it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_luv_age.103: Depending on the recipes you may also need a much larger Input Bus to handle the amount of items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.1: I'm not about to explain how the entire GregTech power system works, but I will point out some of the basic starter machines and some useful information that will make you life much easier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.2: The most important thing to know is to always match your tiers of energy. LV Cables for LV machines and Turbines, MV for MV and so on. Providing more energy than a Cable can accept will burn the Cable out. Providing more energy than a machine can accept will blow up the machine.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.3: Consumes 64 mb/t of Steam to produce 32 EU/t. This means if you are using High Pressure Steam Solid Boilers, you will require 5 in order to keep 1 Basic Steam Turbine Generator running.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.4: Highly advised to have a buffer for Steam, as in a Drum or Tank, with the highest capacity you can afford, or go right for the Large Bronze Boiler.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.5: The first few machines you should make are the Basic Wiremill, the Basic Bender, and optionally the Basic Extractor, and Basic Fluid Solidifier. These will help you craft basic components much easier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.7: Can process Ingots into Wires and Wires into Fine Wires.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.8: Some Ingots will be processed directly into Fine Wires as they do not have a Wire.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.10: Can process materials into Plates, Foils, and Springs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.11: This is the go to machine for Plates and Foils, making 1 Plate per 1 Ingot and 4 Foils per 1 Ingot.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.13: Can extract items into liquids and other items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.14: Mostly used for liquid metals, but Liquid Glass is required for Diodes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.16: Uses Casting Molds to solidify liquids.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.17: The Casting Molds are not consumed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.19: Think of this as an electric Crafting Table, that can also accept stacks (or less) of items, and fluids.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.20: If something can be crafted in a normal Crafting Table and an Assembler, the Assembler recipe is normally cheaper or more efficient in some way.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.21: There are many items that can only be crafted through the Assembler. If you find yourself adding and removing fluids constantly, it is a good idea to have a designated Assembler per fluid type required, as in 1 stocked with Rubber, 1 stocked with Glue, and so on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.22: If the craft isn't working then chances are it either needs to be set to a certain circuit value, or requires a higher tier Assembler, pay attention to the EU/t cost.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.23: These are normally the most expensive machines to craft.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.24: Assemblers are crucial to progression. You will require at least 1 of each tier, sometimes more.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.26: The Electric Blast Furnace (called EBF from now on) is a crucial multiblock that will be used forever. The Energy Hatches will determine the EU/t the EBF can use, and the Coils determine the heat that can be used.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.27: &2It is highly advised to be using a Large Bronze Steam Boiler by now due to the amount of Steam required to power the EBF.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.28: Throughout your playthrough you will be upgrading the Energy Hatch and Coils to higher tiers to process higher tier materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.29: You will require having an MV energy rating to create Aluminium Ingots which may seem impossible at first, just use 2 LV Energy Hatches at first. &nHaving 2 Energy Hatches of a certain tier will increase the EBF to the next tier&r. For example, 2 LV Energy Hatches will allow you to do MV recipes. Each Energy Hatch can accept 2 amps of energy. This is how you will need to increase tiers of the EBF each time. Keep in mind it will take 4 Basic Steam Turbine Generators to power an EBF with an MV energy rating. Since Aluminium Ingots require 120 EU/t and your 4 generators will produce 128 EU/t, you must have an energy loss in Cables of less than 8 EU. Keep your generators as close to the Energy Hatch as possible to avoid energy loss.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.30: &2If you are struggling to run the EBF for the first time, see the next page of this quest using the arrow [->] at the bottom right of this quest window for a more detailed guide on Energy Hatch, Cable/Wire, and Steam transfer setups.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.31: This will really start to test your EU production and Steam transfer, you may need to have a decent EU storage buffer for your first few Aluminium Ingots, but relying on an EU buffer to run your EBF is not really viable long term.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.32: You will end up having more than 1 EBF if you don't want to reconfigure the setup for various recipes, some recipes require different fluid inputs. Advised to make passive setups for tiered ingots like Steel, Aluminium, Stainless Steel, and so on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.33: Read the Multiblocks quest for more information regarding multiblocks in general.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.34: Other quests for multiblocks from now on will only have the controller block as a quest objective as they are all usually very flexible in setup.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.37: Each Energy Hatch can accept 2 amps in. Each Steam Turbine generates 1 amp.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.38: Aluminium Ingots require 120 EU/t. Each Steam Turbine generates 32 EU/t.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.39: Each Energy Hatch Requires 2 Steam Turbines each to be connected to them to get at most 64 EU/t to each Energy Hatch, for a total of 128 EU/t.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.40: Cables \& Wires have an energy loss per block travelled, this is seen in the tooltip for the Cable or Wire.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.41: Try to position the Steam Turbines 1 block away from the Energy Hatches, so there is only 1 block worth of Wire or Cable, allowing for the least amount of energy loss.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.42: That should be good for the Energy Hatch, Steam Turbine, and energy transfer portion.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.43: You may still be having issues, but first check if you are having issues due to Steam transfer rates, as in, are the Steam Turbines running low/empty of Steam. If they are, it is now a transfer rate issue.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.45: If you are still having issues, it is most likely due to Steam transfer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.46: Steam burns at a rate of 2 mB of Steam per 1 EU generated. So this means for 1 Steam Turbine to generate 32 EU/t, that requires 64 mB/t of Steam. So for 128 EU/t that requires 256 mB/t of Steam.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.47: You may be making enough Steam, but not transfering it fast enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.48: With Potin Pipes, you would need at least a Large Potin Pipe to transfer enough steam through 1 Pipe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.49: The Pipe transfer rate is one thing, but another is how you are pushing/pulling the Steam into the Pipe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.50: An LV Electric Pump only has a transfer rate of 64 mB/t, meaning just one of those pushing Steam into the Pipes would not be enough.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.51: Using just 1 Ender Tank or Dimensional Tank on auto output is also not powerful enough to handle all 4 Steam Turbines, however 1 Dimensional Tank is powerful enough for 2 LV Steam Turbines, so you could use 2 Dimensional Tanks for 4 LV Steam Turbines. Ender Tanks have a slower auto output rate.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.52: If using AE2 to transfer Steam, you may need Acceleration Cards to export more Steam.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.53: An Ender Fluid Conduit has a base extraction speed of 200 mB/t so it is close, but not quite enough. You could either just add another extraction point for the Ender Fluid Conduits, or use an Extraction Speed Upgrade.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.54: If your Steam is being stored in a Super Tank and the Super Tank is auto outputting into the Pipes, that should be fast enough as they have a rather high output rate.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.57: Aluminium is the main material for the MV Age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.58: While you don't need to obtain Aluminium Dust as a byproduct, it may be easier than an ore processing line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.59: Sapphire Dust in an LV Electrolyzer is a decent way to get your first Aluminium Dust, and Clay Dust in an MV Electrolyzer is another decent way when you have an MV Electrolyzer as Clay Dust is easy to obtain in this pack, and the byproduct of Silicon Dust is nice to have too.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.60: Aluminium Dust can come from many things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.62: Just like your first Circuits being used for LV recipes, these will be used for MV recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.63: Be sure to keep an eye out for easier Circuit recipes as you progress through ages as each tier of Circuits has multiple types available that are usually easier/cheaper to make.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.64: Look into the Circuit Assembler in order to make Circuits much cheaper.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.66: Can process things into Rods, Screws, and more.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.67: The go to machine for Rods, making 2 Rods per Ingot.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.69: The way crafting machines works in GregTech looks very complicated at first but there is a method to it. Crafting components are used A LOT, like Electric Motors and Electric Pistons and such.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.70: If you look you will notice there are different tiers of components, like LV, MV, HV, and so on. Higher tier machines and components are usually almost an identical craft, just using higher tier materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.71: Try not to ever craft just 1 when it comes to crafting components, you're going to need a lot of them anyways, even in higher tiers you will still end up making lower tier machines for certain things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.72: Note: Electric Pumps, Conveyor Modules, and Robot Arms can also be used as a Cover. See Covers quest for more information on Covers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.75: Covers do not take up a block space, instead they are installed on the side of a block, helping with compact setups.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.76: Certain things can be installed on machines or pipes as a Cover, allowing more automation and features without having extra blocks or Pipes. To edit a cover you need to use a Screwdriver, to remove a Cover you need to use a Crowbar.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.77: Almost any machine or block from GregTech can have a Cover applied, like basic machines, Pipes, Drums, Super Tanks, and more.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.78: An item's tooltip will state if it can be used as a Cover. Because of this you may search EMI for "cover" and see all available Cover options.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.79: Something to note is an Item Filter and a Fluid Filter can be inserted in a Cover to allow filtering.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.82: Cuts things, like blocks into Plates, Logs into 6 Planks, and many other things. Gem Plates are always made from a block in a Cutter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.83: Cutters are crucial for Circuit crafting as well as they are required to cut all Boules into Wafers, and Engraved Wafers into Chips.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.84: Cutters always use a fluid with every recipe, which is always a choice of either Water, Distilled Water, or Lubricant. Lubricant being half the duration of Water, and Distilled Water having a duration in the middle of Lubricant and Water.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.86: Has a variety of uses, can mix items and fluids together.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.88: Can store Batteries which in turn can store EU. There are 4x, 8x, and 16x versions which hold up to that many Batteries, allowing more EU storage.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.89: Powering a Battery Buffer that holds Batteries will charge the Batteries, and extracting EU from the Battery Buffer will draw EU from the Batteries inside.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.90: Each Battery in the Battery Buffer that has EU to provide will provide 1 amp, meaning a 4x Battery Buffer filled with Batteries will provide 4 amps, and a 16x Battery Buffer filled with Batteries will provide 16 amps. This is important to determine which Cables you require. So for a 4x Battery Buffer you should be using a 4x Cable, and so on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.91: While Battery Buffers can only output a maximum amperage of how many Batteries they can hold, they can actually receive in twice the amount, so a 4x can accept 8 amps in.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.94: Has a few uses but mostly used to craft Batteries.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.95: Batteries can be inserted into a Battery Buffer, or directly into a machine in the "Charger Slot" if you wish, this will draw EU from the Battery if needed instead of requiring a direct EU source. They can also be used to charge portable items by enabling the discharge mode.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.96_1: More information on Batteries themselves can be found in the
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.97: Note that Batteries are completely optional. If your power generation is good enough, you don't need to store it, just generate it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.99: This block will convert EU into FE, or FE into EU.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.100: 1 EU converts into 4 FE and 4 FE converts into 1 EU.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.101: Use a Soft Mallet to change the conversion mode.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.102: Note that AE2 can mostly be handled by the starter Creative Energy Cell, however you can also craft them, you don't need Converters for separate AE2 systems, but you can.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.103: GregTech EU can power FE related blocks, but not the other way around, just run energy to the FE block with normal GT Cables/Wires.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.106: Your first Diodes will have to be crafted using Gallium, which is a byproduct of Sphalerite.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.107: There are a few ways to produce Gallium Dust from Sphalerite, but one of the better methods would be Spahlerite Ore -> Forge Hammer, Crushed Sphalerite -> Thermal Centrifuge for 33% chance of Gallium Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.108: Arsenic Dust can easily be obtained from Realgar Dust in a Centrifuge.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.109: You will be using these in Circuits until you can craft the SMD Diodes in the HV age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.113: Splits things into their periodic table elements.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.114: If you see an element in a tooltip that you want, you can most likely obtain it through the Electrolyzer. You'd be surprised what is in a Clay Ball.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.115: Electrolyzers often play a big part in obtaining certain resources from base materials, they will be used a lot throughout the pack.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.117: Splits things into many other things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.118: Will be required to get your first Glue which is needed for the Phenolic Circuit Boards.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.119: It is not a bad idea to have designated setups for Centrifuging both Rubber Logs and Sticky Resin as the byproducts are going to be useful for a variety of things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.121: Magnetizes things without the need for Redstone Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.122: While Iron Rods can be magnetized with Redstone Dust, Steel Rods and others cannot.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.124: While it has some other uses, it is mainly used to process gem dusts into gems.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.125: This is also how you can easily convert GregTech Certus Quartz into AE2 Certus Quartz Crystals if you need to for some reason.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.127: Has many uses but early on can be used for efficient Rubber production.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.128: GregTech is very big on chemicals and mixing chemicals, however they can usually be done in an LV Chemical Reactor. Autocrafting highly advised.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.130: You may be used to inserting a Programmed Circuit with a certain number into a machine for recipes, this system now uses a Ghost Circuit. Since the machines are all crafted with Circuits, why insert another?
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.131: On the left side of a machines GUI there is a Circuit Settings tab where you can select the Circuit number you wish without actually inserting a Programmed Circuit.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.132: Newer feature! You can now use your mouse scroll wheel while hovering over the Ghost Circuit spot to change the setting by scrolling.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.135: &n&l&6DON'T EVER BUILD A MULTIBLOCK ACROSS CHUNK BORDERS! PRESS F3+G TO SEE CHUNK BORDERS!&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.136: Multiblocks all share a common pattern, the main block, structural blocks, Input/Output Buses, Input/Output Hatches, Energy Hatches, Muffler Hatches, and Maintenance Hatches. Some may have other unique blocks. Some require certain tiers of Hatches and Buses, some do not matter what tiers you use.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.137: The main block: The block you interact with (controller), usually has the name of the multiblock you are building. Always has to be in the exact spot to function.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.138: Structural blocks: Filler blocks (often a type of "Casing") used to fill in the rest of the shape of the multiblock. Can usually be changed around with Hatches or Buses.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.139: Buses: Handles the importing and exporting of items. Will automatically interact with adjacent inventories. Can usually be changed around with Hatches or structural blocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.141: Input/Output Hatches: Same as the above but for fluids.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.142: Energy Hatches: Same as the above but for EU. Almost all multiblocks can accept 2.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.143: Muffler Hatch: Will collect waste after a while. Cannot block the exhaust side.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.144: Maintenance Hatch: Perform maintenance with various tools. Can be automated later on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.145: Coils: Coils are in special multiblocks and if there are Coils, then you can upgrade the tiers for bonus rates. Effects different multiblocks in different ways. Always has a set position in the structure that must be the Coils. All Coils in a multiblock must be the same tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.146: You can typically change the position of any Buses, Hatches, and structural blocks around but there is usually a minimum requirement of structural blocks, some multiblocks require fluids and items and some only require one or the other. The main block and Coils always have to be in a set location.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.147: You can upgrade an Energy Hatch to a higher tier to increase the tier/speed, and you can almost always add a second Energy Hatch to do the same. Having 2 MV Energy Hatches will in turn make it run at HV, as long as you feed it the proper energy.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.148: A note on Muffler Hatches and Maintenance Hatches. You can't export from the Muffler Hatches in any way but it also doesn't matter if it fills up anyways. Maintenance Hatches need to be "maintained" when you first place the block down. Most multiblocks last a very long time before needing any maintenance. If your multiblock has stopped working, check the Maintenance Hatch for issues. Look at the tooltip in the slot in the GUI for more information.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.149: With all of this being said, multiblocks are quite flexible in how you can set them up so the quest pages will often just have the controller block. See the EMI page for more information on each multiblock by checking the uses on the main block (controller) and you can see how it can be setup.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.152: Note that the ME Annihilation Plane from AE2 is faster, and easier, and all around probably a better option.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.153: Can be used to break blocks, most importantly, ores. If the internal inventory is not full then it will collect the drop, if it is full then the drops will fall in the world. Apply a redstone signal for it to operate.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.154: A great way to obtain Raw Ores intead of ores if you want. Even the LV version is quite fast, definately faster than mining. While it probably won't see much use, it's not bad for obtaining random ores from the Random Ore Generator if you're missing some and don't want to manually mine.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.155: You want the Block Breaker facing an ore that is being generated. Extract the items from the Block Breaker using any means and either keep all the dust types or just send them to a Trash Can.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.157: A simple way to put it, the power scaling from tier to tier will cost 4 times the energy to go 2 times faster. To power an MV machine with LV Steam Turbines will require 4 LV Steam Turbines. However you cannot just add lower tier generators together and produce higher tier energy. For that you need a Transformer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.158: A Transformer can be used to change 4 amps of a lower tier energy to 1 amp of a higher tier energy, and the opposite, 1 amp of higher tier energy to 4 amps of lower tier energy. This behaviour can be changed by using a Screwdriver on it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.159: While this is possible, it is usually best to keep your energy tiers separate.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.162: While there is a Steam version of the Rock Crusher available, I am going to display the LV version as you probably wont be using a Steam version.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.163: The Rock Crusher usually requires Water and Lava (sometimes Water and Water) to be placed in the world, touching the machine. Insert a catalyst in the GUI slot and it will generate a certain block type. The fluids and input catalyst are not consumed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.164: The Rock Crusher can produce anything the Infinite Block Generator can copy as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.166: While you don't need Steam powered machines anymore, you are techincally still using Steam to generate EU using a Steam Turbine.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.167: I will point out some basics about the GregTech power system along the way but if this is your first time playing with GregTech then I highly advise reading a wiki or watching a video explaining it as there is too much going on to explain here.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.168: Too much energy given to a machine will cause it to explode.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.169: Too much energy given to a Wire or Cable will cause it to burn up.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.170: Not giving enough energy to a machine will reset the progress.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.171: Most multiblocks can have 2 Energy Hatches, which increases the tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.172: Wires and Cables can only carry so many amps (like channels) of energy. Running 4 machines at once will require 4 amps.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.173: Transformers can be used to go up or down an energy tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.174: There are too many ways to power your base to even mention.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.175: For each energy tier you increase, generators will generate 4 times the energy at 4 times to consumption rate, and machine speed is 2 times faster.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.178: If you are new to GregTech there are some things you should know about the mod in general. There is more information in the "New To GregTech" quest chapter but here is a semi quick breakdown. For more information see the "New to GregTech" quest chapter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.179: Take your time - With an exception for the Steam age, don't rush through progression. If you do you are going to suffer from lack of infrastructure and automation. Once you get to the LV age you should start looking into automating as much as you can with AE2. Being able to request Circuits from your Terminal is going to be a game changer. As you progress into higher ages you should be looking to replace your autocrafting machines with higher tier machines to double the speed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.180: Amps - How many channels of energy a Wire or Cable can carry. A single block machine will either generate or use 1 amp of energy. The easiest way around this is the use a Battery Buffer. The 4x means to Battery Buffer can hold 4 Batteries. A Battery Buffer will send out the same amount of amps as the amount of filled Batteries it contains, meaning a filled 4x Battery Buffer will send out 4 amps, even if you only have 2 generators. You will need Cables to match the amperage or else the Cables will burn up.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.181: Energy tiers - GregTech is devided into energy tiers. You start in the Steam age with no energy, however Steam will still be how you produce energy for now. As you progress through tiers something important to note is that you will start going through fuels 4 times faster as you are generating 4 times the energy. Machines will operate 2 times faster. Steam will hold up to the LV and MV age quite well but every couple tiers you increase you will want to look for a better fuel option. For instance when I reached the HV age the Steam consumption rate was just too much so I looked into Oil processing for Diesel to use in Combustion Generators.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.182: 1 generator per machine - This is not overkill, especially with unlimited resources, even more so if a recipe requires almost all of the EU/t that the generator makes. A lot of recipes will take 30 EU/t where an LV Steam Turbine only produces 32 EU/t. Just give the 1 machine a dedicated generator to make sure it will always run, especially for certain autocrafting setups that cannot afford to stop. Now obviously if you have 4 machines that all need 4EU/t then a Cable setup is ideal.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.183: Energy loss per block - Wires and Cables have an energy loss per block. This is mostly an issue in the earlier ages as losing 1 eu per block is quite damaging with not much eu to spare. In later ages you will be able to span greater distances with Cables because the EU/t being generated is usually much more than the EU/t required by machines. There are also "Superconductor Cables", 1 for each energy tier, which do not lose any energy per block. They are quite expensive but very worth it in certain situations. You should always be trying to craft the Cables for you energy tier with the lowest loss per block that you can afford.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.184: Mobs - You don't need any mobs but some may help. GregTech pretty much ignores all mob drops in the first place, and Netherite for that matter. There are still ways to make crazy mob farms with Apotheosis and Mob Grinding Utilities, but you can play the pack on Peaceful Mode if you wanted. I even trivialized food too so there isn't much difference. With the only real mob drop being used being Ender Pearls, Ender Pearl Dust is craftable from ore resources.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.187: The LV Superconductor, has a loss of 0 EU per block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.188: There is a Superconductor Wire for each energy tier that always has 0 EU loss per block. They normally use a unqiue metal made in the EBF.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.189: They also usually have a higher amp rating than other wires of the same size, for example this 1x Wire has 2 amps.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.190: They come in all the standard Wire sizes. There are no Cable versions, but the Wires do not cause damage when touching them.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.191: Note that to craft each tier of Field Generator (crafting component), the respective tier of Superconductor is required. While earlier tier Field Generators are not required for progression, from IV and upwards they will be, meaning so will the Superconductors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.193: The only purpose Manganese Phosphide Ingots have are to make LV Superconductors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.194: This is a common pattern with Superconductor materials in each age. The Superconductors themselves can sometimes be used in crafting other things (Field Generators always use Superconductors of that tier), but the material used to make the Superconductors never have other uses so you are safe to turn them all into Wires.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.196: Process Manganese Dust and Phosphorus Dust in an LV Mixer to obtain Manganaese Phosphide Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.197: Both are byproducts of other resources. Look through EMI to see what suits you best.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.227: Apotheosis Gem crafting and upgrading, in a GregTech way.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.231: Cutting Board from Farmer's Delight with bonus outputs.

Will process any ore blocks as if they were a nether or end ore variant, doubling the natural output. Coke or Coke Dust cuts processing time down by 25%. Steam Oven and others are still better to use when available.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.235: Certus Quartz Charger from AE2, can use AE2 or GT Certus Quartz, very fast.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.239: End game "I win" multiblock if you so choose to build one.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.241: Makes many types of glass with base inputs (Sand + Oxygen + specifics).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.243: Most farmable things like trees and crops, fast, decent outputs, does not consume inputs.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.245: Makes AE2 Processors very fast with base inputs, skipping creation steps.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.247: Kind of like a super advanced Simple Ore Generator, outputs 1 stack per iteration.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.249: "Simulates" animal breeding and killing, for animal meats.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.251: Generates fluids you would normally find in world.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.253: A simulated mob farm in a multiblock manner, insert a Spawn Egg of a mob as a non consumable input, some other inputs, roll either the whole loot table or select specific drops.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.256: One for each tier from LV to IV, each tier increasing in movement speed and jump height.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.257: LV grants 20% speed boost, MV 40%, HV 60%, EV 80%, IV 100%.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.258: All tiers give the same level of step assist, allowing you to step up one block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.259: You can toggle the jump height on or off by holding them and sneak right clicking.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.260: Can be equipped in a unique Curio slot.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.262: Paired with Concrete (from GregTech) you can move around quite quickly.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.264: A basic multiblock that runs off Steam and performs up to 8 Wiremill recipes at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.265: Cannot be upgraded to run faster or do more parallels at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.266: The Large Wire Factory later on is a much better version.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.267: Not great for autocrafting setups but great for bulk crafting.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.268: You can set the Programmed Circuit value in the Input Bus.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.269: Up to 8 Wiremill recipes at once!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.271: Increases your movement speed while walking or running on them.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.272: There are 14 decorative variants of each of the 3 colors of Concrete from GregTech. The different types of light/dark/darker do not have any speed increase differences, just aesthetic.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.273: You will need Liquid Concrete later on for progression related things anyway so it may be worth it to get a head start and be able to move faster.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.274: It's fairly cheap to produce and has a few mixing options from easy to obtain dusts and Water.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.275: First you make Light Concrete, and it can be processed again into Dark Concrete, then processed again into Darker Concrete.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.276: Paired with the Exoskeleton Legs you can move around quite quickly.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.279: The Phenolic Printed Circuit Board is the first Circuit Board upgrade. As you move into new Circuit lines, new Circuit Boards will be used.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.280: You can either go the route of using Silver Wires, Sodium Persulfate, or Iron III Chloride. The Sodium Persulfate can be used in some ore processing chains to get certain byproducts easier but any option is viable for now.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.281: Note that every Printed Circuit Board upgrade in later ages will use the same Sodium Persulfate or Iron III Chloride routine, and they will not have a Wire related recipe anymore, so you will eventually need to go one of the chemical routes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.282: You will always need double the Sodium Persulfate compared to Iron III Chloride, this may seem trivial earlier on but in later stages the difference does become quite large.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.284: Can be equipped in a unique Curio slot.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.286: Right click to open the GUI for filtering.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.287: Sneak right click while holding it to enable or disable.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.288: Will not magnetize items if you are sneaking.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.290: Field Generators are tiered crafting components. The earlier tiers don't see too much use, but higher tiers start to see more use.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.291: Field Generators are always crafted using 4 of the 4x Superconductors of the matching tier up to IV.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.292: After IV they still use Superconductors, but in the form of Fine Wires.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.294: Place down the Barterer and place a Piglin inside.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.295: You can get a Piglin as an item a few ways, either buy one directly from the Market, buy a Piglin Spawn Egg from the Market, or sneak right click on a "not busy" Pigin in the world (non aggressive or not transforming). You can find Piglins in the Nether, but it might be easier to just buy the item version directly.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.296: Insert Gold Ingots into the Barterer and the Piglin inside will take a Gold Ingot and generate barter items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.297: Sneak right click to remove the Piglin.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.298: A decent source of Ender Pearls, Nether Quartz, Glowstone Dust, String, Obsidian, and more.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.300: Place down the Trader and place a Villager inside.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.301: You can get a Villager as an item by sneak right clicking on one in the world. You can buy a Villager Spawn Egg from the Market.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.302: You also need to insert a job station, like a Barrel, Cauldron, Lectern, Charger (AE2), and so on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.303: The Villagers still need to restock trades, and do so 2 times per day.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.304: The Villagers also level up as normal while trading with them, a cured Villager will apply the trade discounts, and you can remove the Villager from the Trader with no harm, they keep all their data.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.305: Sneak right click to remove the Villager.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.306: Look into the Converter if you want to cure Villagers using a similar block. You still need the Potion of Weakness and Golden Apple, but it can be done inside a Converter block to make it easier if you want.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.307: With access to Forged Netherite you can make the Auto Trader.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.309: See the Multiblock Info tab by checking the uses for the Large Bronze Boiler in EMI for exact number of blocks and setup as it can be slightly modular depending what fuel source you use (solid or liquid).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.310: The Large Bronze Boiler produces 800 mB/t of Steam. The Basic Steam Turbine Generator uses 64 mB/t to produce 32 EU/t. A single Large Bronze Boiler can support 12.5 Basic Steam Turbine Generators running constantly.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.311: You can either use solid or liquid fuels, but you still require a Water input. Both are viable but it may be easier to feed it with Lava as it can be easier to obtain.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.312: Fuel is consumed rather quickly to produce up to 800 mB/t of Steam.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.313: The Large Bronze Boiler consumes 100 mB of Lava every 11 seconds. The Large Boilers have had their &afuel consumption rates drastically lowered&r compared to older GregTech versions and are much more reasonable now.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.314: 1 Basic Lava Generator is more than enough to keep up with the consumption rate.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.315: 1 Basic Water Generator is more than enough to keep up with the comsumption rate.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.316: &6&nDO NOT provide fuel without Water or it will explode.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.317: There are higher tier multiblock boilers available that produce more Steam.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.318: As this is probably one of your first muiltiblocks with a Maintenance Hatch, you should know about them. When you first place down a Maintenance Hatch it will need to be "maintained" with certain tools. Open the Maintenance Hatch and hover over the icon to the top right to see the issues. Left click in the main slot in the interface with the correct tools in your inventory to "maintain" the Maintentance Hatch. This needs to be done the first time you place down the Maintenance Hatch and again many hours down the road. If a multiblock requires maintenance then it will stop working. An easy way to get all the correct tools is to just get out whatever tools were required to craft the Maintenance Hatch. There are ways to help with or prevent this later on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.319: If you want more information on multiblocks in general, you may want to check out the Multiblocks info quest.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.320: So much Steam! (and no more random explosions!)

sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.326: It also required XP that can be taken from you when crafting.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.327: Most standard Enchanted Books can be crafted using this, except for some Apotheosis Enchantments and the higher than normal level standard Enchantments added by Apotheosis as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.328: The &aStable Footing&r Enchantment can be made using the Enchanter and it allows you to &amine at normal speeds while flying&r.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.330: Power Units can be made using any of the 3 Battery choices, being Sodium, Lithium, or Cadmium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.331: When making a powered tool using one of the Batteries, the storage size of the Battery determines the storage size of the tool.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.332: Lithium is the best and easily obtainable from Lithium Ores so you may as well use that.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.333: Power Units are used to craft any of the powered tools.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.334: There are LV, MV, HV, EV, and IV Power Units. The recipes for the tiered powered tools are always the same, except the tier of the Power Unit used determines the tier of the powered tool crafted.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.336: There are 3 LV Batteries available, but Lithium is the best as it holds the most EU, so there isn't really a reason to use another type.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.337: While Batteries are used in crafting most hand items that can hold an EU charge, they can also be used to charge items that require EU in your inventory, equipped items, and Curio slots.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.338: By default they are in disabled mode, meaning they won't charge anything. Sneak right click while holding a Battery to enable "Discharge Mode", allowing charging of your items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.339: While there is a Turbo Charger machine available, any powered item from GregTech (and most FE items) can be placed in the "Charger Slot" of a machine that is at least the same tier as the item. Meaning a powered MV item would need to go in at least an MV machine. The Turbo Charger just charges things faster but is not required.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.345: Powered tools use EU instead of durability, unless they are out of EU, then they will use durability.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_lv_age.346: You can craft the tool with a different material tool head to change the material instead of making new ones. This only changes the material stats, not the voltage tier.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_new_to_gregtech: GregTech has a lot going on, if you are new to GregTech take some time to look over the following informational quests.

The basic idea of the mod is to progress through the different "Voltage Tiers", otherwise known as "Ages". Each voltage tier will have a few things in common. You always need to produce a new ingot type and a new Circuit type in order to progress. Each voltage tier uses a lot of a specific ingot type and Circuits of that tier for every machine of that tier. There are some other staples for each tier as well, but if you are new to GregTech then it is best to focus on the ingots and Circuits for now.

You start off using hand tools in many crafting recipes, quickly progressing into Steam power, then into multiple different tiers of electrical energy (voltage tiers/ages). Keep in mind any recipe that uses hand tools can be made in a machine of some kind when you get access to them, by LV you generally don't require any hand tools for crafting anymore, but some still see in world use like Wire Cutters, Wrenches, and a few more.
The energy system in GregTech is NOT like FE or RF you are used to in other mods.

As this modpack contains very easy ways to obtain infinite resources, everything from start to finish for any product can be 100% automated. Keep this in mind as you progress, the more complete automations you setup the better off you will be in the long run.

If you are unfamiliar with Applied Energistics 2 (AE2), you may want to focus on getting the hang of that sooner than later. GregTech is very big on "micro crafting", meaning a recipe for a machine or item typically has many other involved recipes for the components to craft the machine or item. AE2 can help simplify this a lot with auto crafting.
Some of this information will be repeated again throughout the quest book, this is a condensed informational page.
Progression!
GregTech Basics

Item and Fluid Pipes require a Wrench to interact with them. When you place one down you may interact with the grid that you see on another Pipe to automatically connect to it, otherwise you need a Wrench to connect/disconnect Pipes.

Different Pipes from GregTech have different transfer rates, and for Fluid Pipes there are different tempurature ratings, as well as if it can handle gases/plasmas/others or not. Different fluids have different tempuratures and some are specifically gases/others, this will be stated in the fluid's tooltip.

Pipes will not automatically import or export things, you can attach a Conveyor (for items) or an Electric Pump (for fluids) and configure it with a Screwdriver in order to do that, or just have a machine auto export into the Pipe.
Use a Wrench!
Wrenches
Pipes

There are a variety of different hand tools that are both used for crafting and in world use. The material the tool is made of only effects the tool's durability and harvest level, some materials come crafted with enchantments. Crafting recipes requiring hand tools usually always have a machine recipe available as well.
Using hand tools to craft will use some durability from the tool, however you can craft unbreakable tools with a couple materials down the road.

Using hand tools to craft within AE2 can be slightly annoying sometimes for one small reason and it has an easy fix. If you have something in the crafting grid in your AE2 system and try to craft something else that requires what is in the crafting grid, it will not see it as in your system. This can be annoying when crafting things requiring tools and they are still resting in the crafting grid from the previous craft. Either just make 2 of each tool so one is always in storage, or get in a habbit of clearing the grid back into storage after crafting something, but honestly having extra of each tool is easier, faster, and you'll need more than one anyways.
Some hand tools can be used in world to edit certain things.

Hammer - Can be used to mute a machine. Harvesting a block in the world will act as if it was run through a Forge Hammer. This allows GT Hammers to be used for obtaining Gravel, Sand, and Dust as well.
Wrench - Can be used to connect or disconnect Pipes, set output sides for machines, set the steam vent side for steam machines, and rotate machines.
Wire Cutter - Can be used to connect or disconnect Wires/Cables.
Screwdriver - Can be used to edit Covers and various blocks like Drums.
Crowbar - Can be used to remove Covers from machines.
More than just crafting!
Hand Tools

GregTech uses crafting components like Electric Motors, Electric Pistons, Robot Arms, and more. These crafting components are used in almost every machine recipe. If you try to craft everything as you need it you will go crazy. Craft these components in bulk and eventually automate them. It is good practice to automate as much as you can from start to finish to make passive lines of products.
The same goes for Circuits, a Circuit is needed for every machine you make and also sometimes used for other components as well.
Having a healthy supply of crafting components and Circuits will same you a lot of time.
For more information on Circuits see the "Progression" quest chapter.
Never just craft 1!
Crafting Components
Tag Filters act a little differently than normal Filters, you can type different commands and text to make more complicated filtering.

Namespacing: Tags are often namespaced for better organization, which means they are prefixed with a domain followed by a colon. For instance, minecraft:ores/iron might be a tag for iron ore. When using tag filters, you'd need to specify the full namespaced tag.

Wildcard *: Wildcards are still used to match any sequence of characters, but you might need to be more specific about where in the tag's hierarchy you're applying it. For example, minecraft:ores/* could match any ore type defined under the ores category in the minecraft namespace.
Exclusion !: To exclude items with certain tags, you would use the exclamation mark. For example, !minecraft:ores/iron would exclude iron ore from the selection.

Combining Conditions: To combine multiple conditions, you might use a logical AND (;) or OR (,), depending on the system. For example, minecraft:ores/iron; !minecraft:ingots/iron could mean "include iron ore but exclude iron ingots."
Combine specific filters!

The GregTech EU system acts very differently than most other energy mods. One thing to keep in mind is you cannot simply add generators together to produce more EU in the same way as most other mods. The EU system works more with electrical channels and amps rather than stacking all EU together to make a big number.
As there are a few topics to go over here, there are different pages in this quest you can cycle through using the arrow buttons in the bottom right corner, or by scrolling with your mouse wheel.
&aTier Progression:&r

GregTech introduces a progression system through different voltage tiers, starting from lower tiers like Low Voltage (LV) and moving up to higher tiers such as Medium Voltage (MV), High Voltage (HV), and beyond.

Each subsequent tier represents a higher power level and allows for more advanced machinery and faster processing times. Many recipes require certain voltage tiers to run, so there is often a minimum tier of machine that can perform the recipe.
&aVoltage and EU:&r

Voltage tiers are measured in units of Electric Units (EU). For example, the LV tier is up to 32 EU/t, MV is up to 128 EU/t, and so on, with each tier quadrupling the maximum EU of the previous tier, while doubling the processing speed.

Because of this scaling system, it is more efficient on EU to make 4 LV machines than 1 MV machine because that turns into *4 EU usage for *4 processing speed, rather than *4 EU usage for *2 processing speed. If you are struggling with EU consumption but still want to scale a production line up you may want more lower tier machines instead of fewer higher tier machines.

If a machine runs out of EU while processing a recipe, it will stop and start the recipe over when it receives more EU. This means you cannot brute force machines that are not receiving enough EU, the recipe will never finish.
&aMachine Compatibility:&r

Machines are designed to operate within specific voltage tiers. If a machine receives EU above its rated tier, it will explode, emphasizing the importance of matching your EU generation and distribution to your machine requirements.

For example, connecting an MV generator that produces 128 EU/t to an LV machine that accepts a maximum of 32 EU/t will cause the LV machine to explode. The same goes for tiered Cables/Wires, providing too much EU to a lower tier Cable/Wire will cause the Cable/Wire to burn, destroying it in the process.
&aTransformers:&r

Transformers are crucial components in GregTech that adapt EU between different voltage tiers. They can step down higher voltages to lower ones for safer use by lower tier machines or step up lower voltages for powering higher tier machines.
Transforming up from LV to MV will require 4 amps of LV to make 1 amp of MV. Transforming down to LV from MV will take 1 amp of MV to make 4 amps of LV.
&aCabling and Loss:&r

Different tiers require different types of Cables/Wires to handle the EU without significant loss. Higher voltage tiers can transmit power more efficiently over long distances, reducing the energy lost in the Cables.
Each voltage tier has a "Superconductor", which has a loss of 0 EU per block. They are normally expensive but worth it. The EU loss per block can be seen in the tooltip for the Wire/Cable.

Other than the EU loss between a Cable and a Wire of the same material there is another difference as well. Wires will cause damage to you if you touch them while they are transmitting EU, Cables are covered versions, which protects against the damage as it is no longer exposed. Superconductors only come in a Wire variant and have no covered Cable version, however they cause no damage because they have no EU loss through the Wire.
Don't blow up your machines!
Voltage
EU Basics

Each Cable/Wire has an amp rating. This determines how many channels of EU your Cable/Wire can carry. A single LV Steam Turbine Generator will generate 1 amp of EU at 32 EU/t. Single block generators only ever produce 1 amp, multiblock generators typically generate more than 1 amp.

Almost all machines that use EU with a few niche exceptions will accept a maximum of 2 amps in. This means even if you have 4 LV Steam Turbine Generators each producing 1 amp at 32 EU/t, a machine that requires 128 EU/t will not accept all 4 amps, it will only accept 2 amps which would be 64 EU/t.

A Battery Buffer is basically the GregTech way of storing EU by inserting Batteries into the Battery Buffer. A 4x Battery Buffer with 4 filled Batteries will send 4 amps when pulling EU from the Battery Buffer, 1 amp for each Battery. This means you can have 1 Steam Turbine (or up to 4) filling a 4x Battery Buffer, and the Batteries will power your machines.

Always make sure you match the amperage you are sending with the proper Cables/Wires. If you send out 4 amps of energy on a 1 amp Cable/Wire, it will burn the Cable/Wire. A 4x Battery Buffer (sending out 4 amps) will require at least a 4 amp Cable/Wire.
Electrical channels!

GregTech and Applied Energistics 2 play very well together. While you start with a basic AE2 storage setup, the rest of the mod basically opens up in with access to the Steam Alloy Smelter, so you will be able to dive right into the rest of AE2 very quickly.

AE2 is not just a storage mod, it is a logistics mod, a storage mod, and above all, an auto crafting mod. If unfamiliar with AE2, learning at least the basics of auto crafting with Patterns is highly recomended.

AE2 handles items and fluids quite well in a variety of ways, it is highly advised to use AE2 for a lot of your logistical needs as well as storage. While using other logistical methods like Pipes or Conduits are nice in certain situations, the bulk of your transfering could be done by AE2 by importing and exporting into and out of your system.
Channels have been set to infinite, meaning there is no channel limit for AE2 Cables.
Many AE2 addon mods are present as well, greatly expanding the capabilities of AE2.
There is an
AE2 quest chapter

containing a basic autocrafting setup and some tips and tricks, but if you require more information on the mod you can see an in game guide on most items by hovering over it with your mouse and holding [G]. There is also a quite detailed guide on AE2 in the modpack's discord, and a ton of information online.
AE2 is your friend!
AE2
Applied Energistics 2

The basic machine interface is pretty self explanitory, item/fluid input and outputs, and usually a slot for a Battery to charge the machine if you want to do it that way instead of running Cables/Wires, not advised but possible.

On the left you will see different tabs. The first tab is the basic machine interface as described above. The second tab is for side configuration, mainly for auto export options. Left clicking on a side will allow items to go out that side of the machine. Left click a couple times to set it to auto, which will auto export outputs if possible. Right clicking will handle fluids in the same way. You can visually see what is going on by items having an orange square and fluids having a blue square. If you want to both input and output from the same side you must make sure the button that allows this is on the correct setting. You will see it within this tab. Likewise you can block inputs from entering the ouput if you wish.
The next tab is usually just the power off and on button, click this to activate or deactive the machine.

The bottom tab is usually the "Ghost Circuit" tab. This can be used to select a Programmed Circuit value needed for a recipe. If you use this then you do not require the actual Programmed Circuit, the Ghost Circuit will handle it. Highly advised using the Ghost Circuits every time a Programmed Circuit value is required. You can also scroll through the values with the mouse wheel without opening the values interface directly.

Some machines may have additional tabs if they are a specific machine that has some extra options, like the Multi Smelter. It can switch between active machine modes, switching from normal smelting recipes to alloy smelting instead. Quite a few multiblocks have this feature where it can switch between different machine modes/recipes, but no single block machines do.
Auto export and more!

sky_greg.quests.chapters_pipes.565: Parallel Hatches more than a single recipe to be performed at once. The duration stays the same as processing a single recipe, but the EU/t, input quantities, and output quantities are all multiplied by &6up to&r the parallel amount.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_pipes.567: &6Not all multiblocks can accept Parallel Hatches&r, but if they can it is stated in the tooltip of the multiblock controller. sky_greg.quests.chapters_processing_line: This chapter will serve as a guide for some more in depth processing lines that don't quite fit into a certain age.
Sometimes quests in other progression chapters will link here if the processing chain is more involved and doesn't full fit into one progression chapter.

Sometimes only the more direct routes will be shown if there are multiple ways to get to a product, sometimes multiple routes will be shown and only 1 route will be required for the quests to progress. However the other routes that are not shown will usually still be mentioned.

The machines that appear between quests in the processing steps are just there to show which machine and the tier of the machine required to do the step. You can check them off manually if you want to help keep track of things but they are also all marked as optional quests. Note that for Chemical Reactors, the LCR is only shown if it is a strict requirement, instead a tiered Chemical Reactor will be shown, even though you can also still use an LCR.
&aSee the next page of this quest for some general tips.&r

- While often not required, Distillation Tower recipes can be very helpful as they give many different fluid outputs at once, often being fluids required in many other processing chains, and that typically include more processing chains to obtain.

- Having fully passive lines for most fluids like the Rubbers and Plastics is a good idea, they don't need to run infinitely, but you generally don't want to have them on autocrafting patterns as there are usually many steps to get the final product and quite a wait time.
- Don't void fluid byproducts, store them for later use, almost every fluid has a valid use.
- You can never have too much Oxygen Gas, Hydrogen Gas, or Sulfuric Acid.
- Setting up dedicated LCRs for some different widely used chemicals is a good idea, like Sulfuric Acid, Methane Gas, and more.
- Circuit 24 on the LCR will usually decrease the amount of machines and processing steps for a product as it uses the base chemicals for the recipe.
Nitric Acid is required for producing the Platinum Sludge Group and required for making the Aqua Regia which is also used in the processing line.

The byproduct of Sulfuric Nickel Solution can be electrolyzed for some Sulfuric Acid and Oxygen Gas. It doesn't really have any purpose so you may as well get some stuff back from it as Sulfuric Acid and Oxygen Gas are constantly used in many processes.

While there are a few ways to produce Nitric Acid, using 1000 mB Nitrogen Gas, 3000 mB Hydrogen Gas, 4000 mB Oxygen Gas with Circuit 24 in an LCR is one of the more straight forward route of producing Nitric Acid.
While there is often multiple routes to get to something in this processing line, the most straight forward routes will usually be shown.
While there are many other things obtained along the way, the primary outputs from the Platinum Line are Rhodium, Ruthenium, Iridium, and Osmium. All which see a large variety of uses.
Besides Osmiridium Dust, everything here can be obtained with IV machines, Osmiridium Dust just requires an LuV Mixer.
Sheldonite, Bornite, Pentlandite, Chalcopyrite, Tetrahedrite, and Chalcocite are all valid options for producing Platinum Group Sludge.
Purified Sheldonite Ore gives twice the output of Platinum Group Sludge than the other options.
Hydrochloric Acid has a variety of ways to produce, but is also a byproduct of making Tetrafluoroethylene so you may have a steady production already.

If you do need a better production, there is a Circuit 24 recipe in the LCR that uses 4000 mB Hydrofluoric Acid, 2000 mB Methane Gas, and 12,000 mB Chlorine Gas to produce 12,000 mB of Hydrochloric Acid, as well as 1000 mB of Tetrafluoroethylene.
Either toss these aside or recycle.
Platinum \& Palladium are required later, but they are also ores so it's not a hard requirement to keep and recycle them.
More steps later in the process will also give some more of these.
Raw Platinum Powder: Platinum Dust \& Chlorine
Raw Palladium Powder: Palladium Dust \& Ammonium Chloride Dust
Platinum Sludge Residue: Silicon Dioxide \& Gold Dust
Used to further process into Iridium.
Later on used to process into Osmium.
Can also be used to process into Nether Star Dust.
Mostly used for RTM Alloy, but also used for more alloys like Ruridit later on as well.
Rhodium Dust comes from Rhodium Sulfate in an Electrolyzer.
You can loop the Sulfur Trioxide byproduct back into making more Sulfuric Acid rather easily.
The easiest way to get Palladium Dust for the Rhodium Plated Palladium is probably Sheldonite Dust in an Electrolyzer, there are a few ways but that is a relatively quick process.
There is Palladium Ore, but it will take a few machines to get the Palladium Dust from it, and Sheldonite Ore smelts directly into the Sheldonite Dust.
While there are quite a few uses for Iridium Ingots, there are also some alloys that require Iridium Dust as well.
A 5:1 ratio of Osmium Tetroxide Dust to Osmium Dust.
While Osmium has some direct uses, it is mostly used to create Osmiridium and HSS-S alloys.
Can be used to make Plastic Circuit Boards more efficiently than Polyethylene, SMD Capacitors more efficiently than Silicone Rubber, and is used in all Cables from EV and up.
A hard requirement for EV Machine Hulls.
Chlorine is rather simple and can easily be obtained from Salt in an LV Electrolyzer.
Hydrochloric Acid is a byproduct from many chemical mixing processes, but can be made pretty simple if needed from Salt + Sulfuric Acid in an LV Chemical Reactor.
The main choice is between Ethylene and Ethane, which are both primarily obtained from Cracked fuels in a Distillation Tower or Distillery. Pick one depending on what route you want to go.
Has many uses, required for many different Circuits, Circuit components, Machine Hulls, and more.

You will want a designated passive production chain setup for this as it is heavily used for a while. There are other fluids later that can basically take the place of Polyethylene for the majority of recipes, but not for a while.
HV Machine Hulls require Polyethylene Sheets, same for EV Machine Hulls, which gets replaced by Polytetrafluoroethylene Sheets for IV Machine Hulls.
The first type of Rubber, aptly named Rubber.
Used in a ton of recipes, required for coating all Wires into Cables up until EV, and many other things.
While Glue isn't technically a type of Rubber, it is kind of used as an early game Rubber before you can actually get your hands on Rubber.

Basically just a Rubber upgrade, while less Silicone Rubber than Rubber is required for lower tier recipes, higher tier recipes will stop accepting Rubber. For example, IV Cables no longer accept Rubber as a valid input, forcing at least Silicone Rubber.

While you aren't required to use Sticky Resin to make Raw Rubber Pulp, it is required to make Glue, and it is also the most viable option for the Raw Rubber Pulp as it gives more output than the alternatives like Rubber Logs, Rubber Saplings, and Rubber Leaves.

The Extractor route is also viable, but you may as well collect the Glue at the same time.

Most things (not all) that use Polyethylene can also be made with Polytetrafluoroethylene with either a lower input cost or boosted output quantity.

Going forward PTFE will be a hard requirement for many things. The LCR itself is basically made from almost all PTFE parts and is crucial to many chemical processes. PTFE is also required for IV Machine Hulls.
When you can, you may want to use the boosted Titanium Tetrachloride recipe.
As a comparison, the boosted recipe uses &a62.5% less Oxygen and 25% less Ethylene&r overall than the standard recipe at the cost of a bit of Titanium Tetrachloride.
You get a lot of excess Hydrochloric Acid from this process, which you can either keep and use for many other things, or recycle back into Chlorine Gas and Hydrogen Gas to loop back into this system.
With an IV LCR you can just use Hydrofluoric Acid, Methane Gas, and Fluorine Gas to directly make Tetrafluoroethylene.
Salt Dust and Rock Salt Dust are the two most direct ways to get Chlorine Gas, with Salt Dust actually being the fastest.
An easy but slow way to get Methane Gas earlier on is Rubber Logs through an LV Centrifuge, but without scaling production any of the early methods are going to be slow.

Carbon Dust and Hydrogen Gas in the LCR can become one of the most direct and fastest ways to get Methane Gas, but not until you can run it at HV, bringing the time down to 10.9 seconds per 1000 mB due to the perfect overclock on the LCR.
There are also many Distillation Tower routes that produce Methane Gas as well.

There are quite a few options for Fluorine Gas, but Bastnasite Dust, Topaz Dust, or Blue Topaz Dust in an MV Electrolyzer are some of the better ways to obtain Fluorine Gas due to the input quantity required, processing times, and useful outputs.

Polybenzimidazole has a wide variety of uses. While it can be used as a fluid substitute in many lower tier recipes to make them cheaper, it also has a lot of required uses in the higher tiers, like Advanced SMD Components and ZPM Machine Hulls.
The only purpose this serves is to make Liquid Polybenzimidazole.
The only purpose this serves is to make Liquid Polybenzimidazole.

Quite a few ways to obtain, the Chemical Reactor recipe of Hydrogen Gas and Nitrogen Gas is one of the more straight forward methods, but you can also obtain Ammonia from Coal Gas or Fermented Biomass in a Distillery or Distillation Tower.

There is an EV LCR recipe as well, but it is a bit more involved and doesn't produce as much output either. The Inputs for the EV recipe may be easier to obtain in larger quantities, but the LV recipe is probably much easier to manage.

With later access to the LCR you can directly mix Sulfur Dust with Water, skipping most of the process.
Phenol has many ways to obtain, the more direct routes being Coal Tar or Wood Tar in a Distillery or Distillation Tower which both can come from an MV Pyrolyse Oven.
While you only require an LV Distillery, if you use the Distillation Tower you can also get the Phenol required for a later step in the chain.
Coal Tar can come from a few things, but the Distillery or Distillation Tower recipes still require products obtained from a Pyrolyse Oven.
As always the Distillation Tower might be more worth it for the extra byproducts as you can also get Ammonia required in a later step of the chain.

Laminated Glass is essentially the new Glass type as of the IV Age, and is also used to make Fusion Glass, Fusion Reactors, the Assembly Line multiblock, and Laser Pipes.

Has quite a few ways to obtain, a few of the more direct routes being in an LV Chemical Reactor using either Carbon Dust, Oxygen Gas, Hydrogen Gas, or Hydrogen Gas and Carbon Monoxide, or even Wood Vinegar in an MV Distillery or HV Distillation Tower.
