The Impure Naquadria Solution goes through an EV Centrifuge and you will get Indium Phosphide Dust, half of your Antimony Trifluoride Dust back, and some Naquadria Solution.
&aSend the Antimony Trifluoride Dust back to make more Fluoroantimonic Acid.&r

To get Naquadah Dust you need to do some ore processing steps, ideally you want to get some of the Enriched Naquadah Dust as well for later on so you don't need to fully depend on the Impure Enriched Naquadah processing here.
Note you can also get some Barite Dust from the ore processing, useful for Barium Dust for the LuV Superconductors.
Fluoroantimonic Acid is Antimony Trifluoride Dust and Hydrofluoric Acid in an HV Chemical Reactor.
Processing Naquadah Dust and Fluoroantimonic Acid in an LuV LCR will produce 3 things, Impure Enriched Naquadah Solution, Impure Naquadria Solution, and Titanium Trifluoride Dust.
Make sure you still have an excess of Naquadah Dust stocked away as you will need quite a bit of standarad Naquadah Ingots still.
&6Also you just need the 1 LCR, not 3 as it may look like it in the processing line chain here.&r
&aYou can get all the Antimony Trifluoride Dust back from processing both the Impure Enriched Naquadah Solution and Impure Naquadria Solution.&r
Antimony Trifluoride Dust is Antimony Trioxide and Hydrofluoric Acid in an LV Chemical Reactor.
Hydrofluoric Acid is Hydrogen Gas and Fluorine Gas in an LV Chemical Reactor, by now you more than likely already have Hydrofluoric Acid being produced from something.
You will also get half back when processing the Impure Enriched Naquadah Solution, and the other half back when processing the Impure Naquadria Solution.
&aYou can get all the Antimony Trifluoride Dust back from processing both the Impure Enriched Naquadah Solution and Impure Naquadria Solution.&r
There are a few ways to obtain Antimony Trioxide Dust, however the simplest most direct route is just Antimony Dust and Oxygen Gas in an LV Chemical Reactor.
Hydrofluoric Acid is Hydrogen Gas and Fluorine Gas in an LV Chemical Reactor, by now you more than likely already have Hydrofluoric Acid being produced from something.

This step really doesn't need to be part of the chain as you can start looping the Antimony Trifluoride Dust around from the Centrifuges back into the Chemical Reactor to make more Fluoroantimonic Acid.
&aYou can get all the Antimony Trifluoride Dust back from processing both the Impure Enriched Naquadah Solution and Impure Naquadria Solution.&r
Not really part of the chain!
You can process in an LV Chemical Reactor with some Calcium to get some Indium Dust and Calcium Phosphide back.
This could replace your old Indium Dust setup.
Trinium is a mix of Trinium Sulfide Dust and Zinc Dust in an LuV EBF with Naquadah Coils.
Trinium is mostly used for Trinium Coils, Naquadah Alloy (the ZPM material), and the UV Superconductors, and has some more uses in its base form.
Trinium is an odd case where the ingot comes before the dust, and the dust is required for some alloys.
While mostly used for the Trinium Coil Blocks, Enriched Naquadah Dust is also used in another alloy for UV Superconductors.

This is not the only way to make the Enriched Naquadah Ingots, you can also get the Enriched Naquadah Dust as a byproduct from ore processing steps for Naquadah Ore and smelt that directly in an EBF as well. This is just a way to get more from the byproducts of the Naquadah Line.

Distilling the Enriched Naquadah Waste can get back some Enriched Naquadah Solution, Naquadria Solution, Sulfuric Acid, and Barium Sulfide Dust. You can loop it back into the earlier steps of the process.
You will need a bit of Zinc Dust as well.
The Impure Enriched Naquadah Solution goes through an EV Centrifuge and you will get Trinium Sulfide Dust, half of your Antimony Trifluoride Dust back, and some Enriched Naquadah Solution.
&aSend the Antimony Trifluoride Dust back to make more Fluoroantimonic Acid.&r
Titanium Trifluoride Dust can be run through an EBF to make Hot Titanium Ingots and also get some Hydrofluoric Acid back.
This could replace your old Titanium setup.
While there is often multiple routes to get to something in this processing line, the most straight forward routes will usually be shown.
While there are many other things obtained along the way, the primary outputs from the Naquadah Line are Trinium, Enriched Naquadah, and Naquadria.
Everything here can be obtained with a ZPM EBF as the highest requirement.
Naquadria is used for the MK II Fusion Reactor, Tritanium Coils, UV Emitters and Sensors, and some other miscellaneous stuff.
A MK III Fusion Reactor can also make Liquid Naquadria, but at first it needs to come from the Naquadria Sulfate Dust.
Distilling the Naquadria Waste can get back some Enriched Naquadah Solution, Naquadria Solution, Sulfuic Acid, and Barium Sulfide Dust. You can loop it back into the earlier steps of the process.

There are 2 final recipes to make Liquid Epoxy, but both are the same inputs in the end. There is a recipe for all 4 fluids and the dust together, and also a recipe for just Epichlorohydrin, Bisphenol A, and dust. The Bisphenol A is just a combination of the Hydrochloric Acid, Acetone, and Phenol.
The recipe using the Bisphenol A is actually faster by a bit, but all inputs and outputs are the same either way.

Even putting that aside, for the Hydrochloric Acid, Acetone, Phenol, and Epichlorohydrin required, all of those fluids have recipes that can also produce another required fluid. Pick your routes around this fact as you can usually make more than 1 required output at a time.
Multiple routes to obtain, pick the one that suits you best due to what you currently have from other processing lines or what seems better.

Epoxy is used to make the Epoxy and Fiber-Reinforced Circuit Boards, which are in turn use to make the Multi-layer Fiber-Reinforced Circuit Boards, which are in turn used to make the Wetware Circuit Boards, which are in turn used to make the Neuro Processing Units, so this will be a big requirement going forward for all Circuits.
LV (LCR required if not using Bisphenol A)
Salt and Water in an LV Mixer, really simple.
Salt Water in an LV Electrolyzer makes 3 Sodium Hydroxide Dust, 1000 mB Chlorine Gas, and 1000 mB Hydrogen Gas.

There are actually 15 uses for Sodium Hydroxide Dust in the LCR, you may want to look through there and see what there is. While you do require the Sodium Hydroxide Dust for Epichlorohydrin, it can also be used to make quite a few other things too, like both Hydrochloric Acid and Phenol at the same time (both also Epoxy ingredients).
Smelt Nether/End Salt Ore into 4 Salt (gem), then put in a Macerator for Salt (dust).
Multiple free Water sources exist by this point.
A simple combination in an LV Chemical Reactor of 1000 mB Hydrochloric Acid, 1000 mB Acetone, and 2000 mB Phenol, which makes 1000 mB Bisphenol A and 1000 mB Diluted Hydrochloric Acid.
This method is actually faster by a bit, but all inputs and outputs are the same either way.
The standard Chemical Reactor has 2 recipes available, and the LCR has 4 recipes available.
There are a few ways to make Epichlorohydrin, but a more direct route is in an LV LCR using 3 Sodium Hydroxide Dust, 4000 mB Chlorine Gas, 1000 mB Propene, and 1000 mB Water.
This will make 1000 mB Epichlorohydrin, and also make 2000 mB Hydrochloric Acid, and 1000 mB Salt Water.
The Hydrochloric Acid will also be required in the Epoxy setup, and the Salt Water can be Electrolyzed for more Sodium Hydroxide Dust.
There are many ways to make Hydrochloric Acid.
If you use the recipe to make Epichlorohydrin that also makes Hydrochloric Acid, you'll have enough for the Epoxy, otherwise a couple of the easier methods are:

2 Salt + 1000 mB Sulfuric Acid in an LV Chemical Reactor makes 1000 mB Hydrochloric Acid, and 7 Sodium Bisulfate Dust, which is also how you make Sodium Persulfate if using that instead of Iron III Chloride.
1000 mB Chlorine Gas + 1000 mB Hydrogen Gas in an LV Chemical Reactor makes 1000 mB Hydrochloric Acid, this is also quite a fast recipe of only 3 seconds.
1000 mB Benzene + 2000 mB Chlorine Gas + 1000 mB Water in an LV LCR makes 1000 mB Phenol (another Epoxy ingredient), 1000 mB Hydrochloric Acid, and 1000 mB Diluted Hydrochloric Acid.
There are 2 Distillery/Distillation Tower recipes, 1 normal Chemical Reactor recipe, 3 LCR recipes, and 1 Fluid Heater recipe.

If you have a Distillation setup for Wood Vinegar already (or want one), this is a decent route as it gives you some Acetone directly and also some Acetic Acid which can be used in an HV LCR with Quicklime Dust (dust not consumed) to make more Acetone as well.

Another option is the direct LCR recipe using 1000 mB Propene, 1000 mB Benzene, 1000 mB Oxygen Gas, and 100 mB Phosphoric Acid, which makes 1000 mB Acetone, and 1000 mB Phenol (another Epoxy ingredient).

There is a similar recipe to the above recipe, using 1000 mB Cumene, and 2000 mB Oxygen Gas, which makes 1000 mB Acetone and 1000 mB Phenol. While the Cumene is still a mixture of Propene, Benzene, and Phosphoric Acid, this route does actually use more Phosphoric Acid and Oxygen Gas in total after mixing the Cumene.
There are also a few rather simple ways to make Acetic Acid, which can be turned into Acetone quite easily.
There are quite a few ways to get Phenol, with 2 recipes being the Distillery/Distillation Tower, and 6 recipes being in the LCR.

If you need it faster, the LCR is probably the way to go, if not in a big rush and just need a passive supply, the Distillation Tower and Pryolyse Oven route may be better because of all the extra byproducts.
Coal Tar and Wood Tar can both distill into Phenol, and can both be made quite easy in a Pryolyse Oven.
Most recipes in the LCR to make Phenol also include either Hydrochloric Acid or Acetone in the outputs too, so you may want to pick a route that makes Phenol as well.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.1: Machine Hulls are used to build machines. There is almost always exactly 1 Machine Hull in a recipe for any single block machine, even some multiblocks use them in their patterns.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.3: The ULV Age isn't really a thing, there are some multiblock parts that are ULV but that's about it. This is mostly so you can run some multiblocks at very low EU rating. There are very few ULV single block machines.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.6: Multiblock Coil Blocks are used in a few multiblocks but most importantly the Electronic Blast Furnace (EBF). In any case where a multiblock has Coils in the pattern, you can increase the tier of Coils for an increased effect.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.7: When used in the EBF, they will increase the maximum heat that the EBF can produce. This will allow for higher tiered Hot Ingots to be produced.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.8: Increasing the tier of Coils you are using on your EBF should always be a priority.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.9: They are always crafted in an Assembler of their same tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.13: Voltage Coils are used in basically every Energy Hatch and Dynamo Hatch. They are ususally not the easiest thing to craft and are crucial for progressing with certain multiblocks, and most importantly increasing energy tiers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.14: They are always crafted in an Assembler of their same tier.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.52: Circuits generally upgrade into other Circuits, but not forever. This chart shows which Circuits will upgrade into other Circuits, and which tiers the Circuits are.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.53: As Circuits are used for everything throughout the mod, this should be helpful to visualize certain Circuit paths.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.54: Each vertical line separates the different tiers. Each Circuit in the same tier can usually be used for anything Circuit related, except upgrading Circuits, that usually requires a specific Circuit type.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.55: More advanced Circuits of the same tier (as in the third LV Circuit) are usually much easier to craft, but not available right away.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.56: Things are slightly more open in the first few ages but once you get to the HV age Circuit paths become a bit more standardized.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.57: Fully automating a Circuit from start to finish will really help you out in the long run.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.58: Top to bottom, left to right!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.60: That's about 2.5 million days, which is almost 7000 years.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.62: You're going to want the best Extruder you can use, not to mention that's a lot of Neutronium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_progression.63: 15 billion EU is not a small amount, make sure you don't run out of energy during the craft or it will restart!

Warp Plates are neat as they don't require interacting with and have no interface.
When you first place one down it creates an Attuned Shard, attuned to that Warp Plate. So if you place 2 Warp Plates down in different spots and swap the Attuned Shards, those 2 will be linked.
Simply stand on a Warp Plate that has its Attuned Shard in another Warp Plate and you will teleport to the other Warp Plate.

If you ever lose the Attuned Shard for whatever reason you can create another one by placing a Flint and 4 Warp Dust in a Warp Plate and it will create another Attuned Shard linked to that Warp Plate.
&aCan also transport items dropped in world on the Warp Plate to the destination.&r

These Facades can cover any Pipes, Cables, and Wires from most if not all mods in the pack. They also work on things like Import Buses, Laser Nodes, and some more things relating to Pipes, Cables, and Wires too.
Craft the empty version and simply craft them together with any block and it will create a Facade for that block type. They also work with connected texture blocks.
You can place a filled Facade back in a crafting grid to get both the Facade - Empty and the block you used to fill it back.

Using any wrench you can sneak right click on the placed Facade to remove it. The Facade Wrench is not needed as any wrench will work, but for example a GregTech wrench will still try to interact with the block behind the Facade and will still change modes when sneak right clicking with it.

While holding the Facade Wrench, any placed Facades will get a "ghost" form, allowing you to see what is behind the Facades, however some shaders can mess with this. You can still usually see a tinting to the Facades, but not actually see through them.

Random Things
sky_greg.quests.chapters_shops_reqs_hidd: You shouldn't be able to see this.
This is where all the quest dependencies for the Shop items are.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.1: Accepts solid fuels and Water to create Steam. Steam is a direct energy source before electricity, and even generating you first electrical energy will come from Steam Turbines. There are many different fuel types available down the road, but for a while it will be Steam. That being said, there are much better Steam sources as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.2: &6If no Water is present and they are heated up they will explode.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.3: Advised you craft &l&nat least&r&r 2 of these (even more will also help).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.4: Steam will &aauto export from the top, back, and sides&r, &6not the bottom or front&r. For this reason it is advised to pump Water in from the bottom and export Steam out of any other side to avoid Steam filling your Water Pipes by mistake.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.5: When you get access to Steel Ingots with the Primitive Blast Furnace you can make some better Boilers, even Solar Boilers which are actually pretty decent.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.6: If you want a large buffer of Steam, look into the Bronze Multiblock Tank quest found below this one, or if you just want a bit of a buffer you can just make some Drums too.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.7: When you can make the Large Bronze Boiler multiblock a bit later, you should do that as soon as you can.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.9: While you don't need Wrought Iron Tools, you may want to use them. They have more durability than Iron Tools.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.10: AE2 can handle tools with any durability for crafting "just fine", just try to have more than 1 of each tool type in the network for less headaches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.11: Most tools need plates which makes crafting Diamond Tools a little gated behind a Cutter, except a Diamond Hammer, that just requires normal Diamonds. Plates made from gems typically require a Cutter, and there is no Steam Cutter so they would need LV machines.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.12: Tools come in the form of many different materials, usually just for higher durability, but some materials come with default enchantments. There are also powered tools for most tool types that use energy instead of durability.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.13: &6Any item with durability can be made unbreakable by using it on a Block of Iridium, this will consume the Block of Iridium. You can also craft Forged Netherite tools which will be unbreakable upon crafting.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.14: &aSee the next page of this quest for more info on what some in world uses of hand tools are. Either scroll the mouse wheel or press the arrow in the bottom right of this quest page to change pages.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.15: While some tools do have additional features not listed here, these are the main features.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.17: - Mute a machine by right clicking on it.

sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.24: - Acts as a Pickaxe to mine machines and Pipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.26: - Connect or disconnect Wires and Cables.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.27: - Acts as a Pickaxe to mine Wires and Cables.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.29: - Edit Covers and various blocks like Drums.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.30: - Change Buses and Hatches from Input <-> Output in world.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.31: - Special interactions with certain machines and multiblock parts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.45: To make a Water Pump for your Steam Boilers you will first need Creosote to make Treated Wood.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.46: Keep in mind the Brick Wooden Form used to craft the Compressed Coke Clay is not consumed while crafting, you only need 1.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.47: The 3 Coke Oven Hatches are optional and allow automation, however if you don't use those then you need 3 more Coke Oven Bricks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.48: Make sure to build all multiblocks within a single chunk, do not let a multiblock machine cross over chunk borders. Press F3+G to see chunk borders.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.49: While all you need currently is the Creosote and it can be made by making Charcoal from Logs, it is highly advised to make Coke from Coal to help with Steel production in the not so distant future.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.50_1: Most multiblocks can share blocks with each other which can save a lot of resources. See the
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.50_3: quest to the left for more detail on that.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.51: &aFor a visual representation of all multiblock setups check the uses of a multiblock controller (the main block) in EMI and there is a page for Multiblock Info which displays a visual guide.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.52: &aAny quest title that shows (M) in the title is just a quick visual indicator that it is a multiblock.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.55: Slowly generates Water, does not actually need a source of Water.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.56: Use Pipes to move the Water where you need. You will need to feed Water into your Steam Boilers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.57: You can upgrade the Output Hatch to increase the amount of Water produced, but you realistically will never need to.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.58: There are easier and better sources of Water later on, this will basically just be used to get through the Steam Age and you probably won't need more than 1.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.59: The Basic Water Generator is available as soon as you have an LV Assembler and is a single block that can handle most Water needs throughout the pack.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.60: There is also an Infinite Water Cover from GregTech which provides blocks it is attached to with infinite Water, and the ME Infinity Water Cell from Extended AE which provides your AE2 system with an infinite Water source.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.63: If somehow you need more, random saplings (and Plant Fiber) can be obtained by harvesting Dirt with a Crushing Hammer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.64: Harvesting a Rubber Tree will also grant Sticky Resin which is used for Rubber early on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.65: You can grow them in a Botany Pot or Primitive Farm as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.67: The main focus of Sticky Resin in the not too distant future is for making Rubber and Resistors. Will be needed in large quantities when making early game Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.68: While you can extract Raw Rubber Pulp from other parts of a Rubber Tree, Sticky Resin gives 3 compared to 1.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.69: Note you can get Sticky Resin from a Botany Pot or Primitive Farm, but harvesting Rubber Trees in world can be significantly faster. If you need a lot fast then just Ultimine a bunch of Rubber Trees.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.71: If you do not have Steam generation yet, see the Low Pressure Steam Solid Boiler quest above.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.72: While some basic alloys like Bronze can be made by hand, some more advanced alloys like Red Alloy Ingots require an Alloy Smelter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.73: All steam machines require an output side which can be set with a Wrench. The output side allows steam buildup to escape. If there is no output side for steam buildup to escape the machine will stop working. Do not block the output side.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.74: If your machine made 1 recipe then stopped, this is why.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.75: Below is an image of an automated Alloy Smelter (for a bit later on), crafting Red Alloy Ingots. You can use a Robot Arm to insert the smelted outputs and supply an exact amount into the Alloy Smelter so it doesn't overfill an input slot with 1 material. You can passively make a lot of alloys this way.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.77: Nuggets to Ingots and Ingots to Blocks cannot be crafted by hand, you need to compress them.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.78: Also required for things like compressing Fireclay Dust into Compressed Fireclay.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.80: While it can do other things, most notably you can make Plates at a 3:2 ratio, still better than a Hammer. For things like Iron Plates you may not care, but for things like Red Alloy and Steel Plates you might.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.81: Another thing to note is the Forge Hammer can crush Cobblestone into Gravel, Gravel into Sand, and Sand into Dust, the same things the Crushing Hammer can do. It may be slower but it can be automated.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.83: Something to note on Circuits, everything revolves around Circuits and they typically evolve into higher tier Circuits. Each Circuit type usually evolves 3 times with some exceptions near the start and end. Every machine you make will require at least 1 Circuit and sometimes up to 4. When crafting Circuits it is a good idea to mass craft as much as you can. Having stacks of Circuits will always be helpful. Each age has their own tier of Circuits and usually grants access to crafting earlier tiers of Circuits easier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.84: Each machine needs on average 2, and the next tier of Circuits requires 3 of this tier Circuit. You will want to automate as much of this as possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.85: Keep in mind certain resources will become significantly easier to process and obtain once you reach the LV age, like Wires in a Wiremill. You may want to make as few of these as possible until you get some new machinery and a basic energy setup.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.86: A tip for some of the first things to use Circuits for would be &3Basic Steam Turbine Generators&r to generate energy in the first place, a &3Large Bronze Boiler&r to produce a lot more Steam than the basic starting boilers can produce, a &3Basic Wiremill&r for much cheaper Wires, and a &3Basic Bender&r for much cheaper Plates. From there you will have everything needed to generate energy and make most Circuit components much cheaper.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.87: Keep in mind resources are infinite and every single step of the process can be 100% automated if you wish.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.88_3: quest page for a visual diagram of how Circuits evolve.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.90: The first source of Steel Ingots, it is slow, and rather expensive to craft, but you may want more than just 1.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.91: Firebricks are no quick task, and you need a lot of them. Steel Ingots can also be made in the Steel Blast Furnace which can be made with some Steel Ingots, and the Electric Blast Furnace (EBF) in the LV Age later on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.92: There are 2 methods of crafting Firebricks. One method uses Water Buckets and empty Buckets in crafting recipes, the other uses a one off steam machine called the Low Pressure Firebrick Mixer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.93: If you want you can do the Water Bucket crafting method and skip the machine, or you can do the machine route and skip the Water Buckets, up to you. The only difference is the Firebrick Mixer route doesn't use any Buckets and instead has a crafting recipe to mix the required dusts together to make Rough Concrete Dust, then you use that in the Low Pressure Firebrick Mixer. The same amount of all inputs are required either way, one just doesn't use Buckets.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.94: &6The Primitive Blast Furnace cannot be automated in any way&r, you must place the inputs in the controller block and take the outputs out from the same place manually. &aThere is a Steel Blast Furnace&r that you can make once you have a bit of Steel Ingots together, and &ait can be automated&r using an Input Bus and Output Hatch. The Electric Blast Furnace (EBF) later in the LV Age uses EU, is much faster, and doesn't require and kind of Coal/Charcoal/Coke anymore.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.96: Crushes many different items into dusts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.97: While a Macerator is not technically required to progress towards a Primitive Blast Furnace, it will be required to get Wood Pulp for your first Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.98: It may still be helpful if you do not have enough Stone Dust from mining. Aside from mining ores that come from Stone ore variants, the Macerator would be required for crushing Cobblestone into Stone Dust. It can also save you a ton of Mortars for the other dusts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.99: &6Note that Macerators do not give byproducts unless using an HV Macerator or higher. Each tier above HV will increase the chances of getting a byproduct.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.101: Grow your crops and trees automatically with a Hopper Botany Pot. Ideal for most resources. While they are rather slow, they are passive and free. There is a multiblock Primitive Farm available basically right away, and a Greenhouse available a bit later for much faster "farming".
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.102: You can use the rewards to automate a Coke Oven for Creosote, or whatever you want but you probably don't quite have access to Rubber yet. A Botany Pot is also a great way to automate Liquid Rubber later on too.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.106: Your first Glass will be in an Alloy Smelter with Glass Dust and a Casting Mold (Block), Casting Molds are not consumed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.107: Glass Dust early on can be made in a shapeless recipe with 8 Quartz Sand and 1 Flint Dust to make 8 Glass Dust, or 1 Quartz Sand and 1 Tiny Pile of Flint Dust to make 1 Glass Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.108: Quartz Sand and Flint Dust can be made either with Sand/Flint in a Macerator, or Sand/Flint and a Mortar.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.110: There are a few combinations you can use to make Steel Ingots at first, but Wrought Iron Ingots and Coke is the fastest.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.111: Steel is going to be used for basically everything throughout the LV Age, just like Bronze was used for basically everything in the Steam age. This will be a pattern going forward for each age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.112: In the not too distant future you can make Steel Ingots with the Electric Blast Furnace (EBF) too.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.113: Note that using the Market block you can buy Spawn Eggs of almost every mob using Steel Ingots as payment.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.115: Raw Rubber Pulp and Sulfur Dust in an Alloy Smelter will make a Rubber Ingot. While Sticky Resin isn't required for the Raw Rubber Pulp, it is much more efficient than other means.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.116: To make the Rubber Sheets you need 2 Rubber Ingots in an Alloy Smelter with a Casting Mold (Plate).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.117: A large amount of Rubber Sheets will be required for Cables. Look into automating Liquid Rubber in the LV age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.119: You have access to Raw Sulfur without needing The Nether.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.120: Required for creating Rubber Ingots in an Alloy Smelter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.122: While this machine has over 400 recipes, we will just focus on 1, Raw Rubber Pulp.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.123: Raw Rubber Pulp comes from basically every part of a Rubber Tree, however Sticky Resin gives the most.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.124: You can easily automate Sticky Resin in a Hopper Botany Pot or Primitive Farm.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.125: Keep in mind that like all Steam machines, a Steam Extractor cannot handle any recipes that involve fluids.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.127: Will generate whatever ore is above it at a rate of 1 per second and place it in its inventory. &6They do not auto output&r into an inventory, in the image the &aDrawers (Sophisticated Storage) have a Puller Upgrade&r to pull from the block above them (which can be crafted at this point).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.128: There is an upgraded version that works at twice the speed, and a multiblock version later on that works at alarmingly fast speeds if you need a crazy amount of ores in the late game.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.129: Advised to set one of these up for each ore you require, to give an infinite supply of each ore.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.130: You can use a combination of blocks from the Simple Resource Generators mod to get an ore where you need it to be. You can also craft specific ore variants using a Raw Ore and the dust of the type you want to make, like 1 Raw Iron + 8 Netherrack Dust. You get a lot of the stone type dusts from early mining so you should have a decent pile of each. You can also make a Silky Quartz Pickaxe that has Silk Touch by default.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.131: &aKeep in mind Nether and End Ores process into twice the output.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.132: Before trying to progress too much you should try to get at least a few of these crafted for the commonly used materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.133: There is also an Assembler recipe that is a decent amount cheaper and faster compared to what is required for the normal crafting recipe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.135: The first form of portable fluid storage available.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.136: Different tiers of Drums have different temperature limits, and some cannot handle gases and other things.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.137: Drums cannot be inserted into from the bottom, but they can be configured with a Screwdriver to auto export from the bottom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.138: You can insert or extract fluids from a machine by trying to place a Drum that contains fluids in the fluid input slot, or trying to place a Drum with space in it in a fluid ouput slot that contains a fluid.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.139: Drums can insert or extract fluids from your AE2 system by left or right clicking on a fluid or an empty spot in your AE2 system.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.141: The second form of portable fluid storage available.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.142: Comes in all of the standard progression materials like Bronze, Steel, Aluminium, and so on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.143: Advised to always have the largest Steam buffer possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.144: Drums cannot be inserted into from the bottom, but they can be configured with a Screwdriver to auto export from the bottom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.146: The third form of portable fluid storage available.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.147: Advised to always have the largest Steam buffer possible.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.148: Drums cannot be inserted into from the bottom, but they can be configured with a Screwdriver to auto export from the bottom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.150: An upgraded Steam Solid Boiler, produces 2.5 times more Steam than the Low Pressure variant.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.152: A basic multiblock that runs off Steam and performs up to 8 Furnace recipes at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.153: Cannot be upgraded to run faster or do more parallels at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.154: The Multi Smelter later on is a much better version.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.155: Up to 8 Furnace recipes at once!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.157: Use your AE2 system for more than just storage and autocrafting. You have more than enough space to be able to use your system as a piping method as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.158: Your AE2 system can store Steam as a fluid, and use Import/Export Busses to move Steam around your base efficiently while not relying on GregTech Pipe transfer rates.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.159: This goes for all fluids, GregTech is very heavy on the use of different fluids and they can be tricky to handle sometimes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.160: See the AE2 quest chapter for some information on basic autocrafting.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.161: There are many AE2 addon mods in the pack, making AE2 incredibly strong in many ways.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.162: Hold [G] while hovering over an item from AE2 to pull up an in game guide.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.165: GregTech Pipes can be quite good in certain situations, in other situations you may want to go for AE2, Modular Routers, EnderIO, or LaserIO, or even Ender Tanks/Chests or Dimensional Tanks/Chests.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.166: A recommendation for early game fluid transport is LaserIO, it is relatively cheap and easy to use. AE2 is still superior but not as easy to access right away. You can even get into AE2 very early on using Villager trades for resources. Look into Easy Villagers if that is the case.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.167: The Covers can make GregTech Pipes quite powerful, they may be kind of clunky and annoying at times, but can be very specific and powerful with certain covers like Fluid Regulators and Robot Arms and such.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.171: The Steam Age is going to be all about using Steam powered machines in order to get your first LV Circuits crafted. Once in the LV Age you will still be using Steam, but to generate electricity instead of directly feeding machines.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.172: Each Steam powered machine has a small internal buffer for Steam but it is advised to have a decent Steam buffer early on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.173: Steam machines require a Steam exhaust port to be set using a Wrench. This will allow a small amount of pressured Steam to escape into the world after each craft. You cannot block the exhaust port or the Steam cannot escape, making the machine stop. Standing in the escaping Steam will also damage you. If your machine did 1 recipe then stopped, this is why.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.174: Steam can be transfered using any fluid transfer method. If using GregTech Pipes, make sure they can handle Gasses and have the proper heat rating. If comfortable with AE2, that may be much easier to manage.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.175: &6&n&lWhen a Boiler is hot and has no Water, it will explode when receiving Water.&r&r&r Always make sure Water is present. This being said, they do not actually consume too much Water.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.176: &6Steam machines cannot handle any recipes that involve fluids as an input or output.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.179: Passively creates Steam from Water and sunlight. While Water is still required, no fuel is required, but is only active during the day and with nothing above it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.180: Available if you want, but the High Pressure variant is a better idea as it basically just uses Steel instead of Bronze, which you already have access to.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.182: An upgraded Steam Solar Boiler, produces 3 times more Steam than the Low Pressure variant.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.184: Most multiblocks can share blocks with each other, often referred to as "Wall Sharing".
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.185: As long as the multiblock structure would still be a valid setup for each multiblock in the wall sharing setup, it should be valid, as in the walls, floors, and ceilings are made of the same blocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.186: In this picture all 4 Coke Ovens are sharing blocks with each other. The ceiling of the bottom level is the floor of the top level and the middle walls are all shared. The center block in this picture is actually being shared by all 4 multiblocks.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.187: Hatches and Buses can often (but not always) be shared as well, allowing for much more compact designs and automation. If 2 multiblocks share the same Input Bus and Output Bus, you can put items in the Input Bus and both multiblocks will run, each pulling inputs for a recpie at a time. The output for both multiblocks would be sent to the 1 Output Bus so you have less spots to collect from.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.188: Depending on the multiblock and how you place things, you can sometimes make large arrays where all multiblocks are interconnected.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.189: Even though you can often share Energy Hatches, it tends to complicate things sometimes due to how the energy system works.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.190: If a multiblock piece specifically says "Multiblock Sharing &4Disabled&r" in the tooltip, they can not be shared, but usually if it does not say &4Disabled&r, it can be shared.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.194: Early Bronze can be crafted by hand with Copper Dust and Tin Dust, which can be obtained by crafting Ingots with a Mortar.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.195: Most alloy dusts that can be crafted by hand have a lower yield than using an Alloy Smelter, but you'll need some stuff to get there first, also most alloys cannot be made by mixing dusts together by hand, they either need an Alloy Smelter or a Mixer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.198: Has one job, to craft Firebricks without using Buckets.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.199: The input amounts of all materials except for the Water is the same as the Bucket crafting route, but you can skip the Buckets if you like by making this and Rough Concrete Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.201: A basic multiblock that runs off Steam and performs up to 8 Macerator recipes at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.202: Cannot be upgraded to run faster or do more parallels at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.203: The Large Maceration Tower later on is a much better version.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.204: Up to 8 Macerator recipes at once!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.206: A basic multiblock that runs off Steam and performs up to 8 Alloy Smelter recipes at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.207: Cannot be upgraded to run faster or do more parallels at once.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.208: The Multi Smelter later on is a much better version.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.209: Up to 8 Alloy Smelter recipes at once!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.211: As the tooltip says, shift/sneak right click on a multiblock controller to automatically build the multiblock. You must have the materials required in your inventory to do so. Just make sure there is nothing in the way.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.212: You can sneak right click on a multiblock controller to see a preview in world of the multiblock structure to see where things will be placed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.213: You may want to move the Hatches and things around after as it will place them in the position of the EMI multiblock preview.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.215: The Inscriber Presses are required to do pretty much anything in AE2. Once you have an Alloy Smelter you can craft them. The Inscriber also requires Red Alloy which would need the Alloy Smelter as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.216: You can convert Certus Quartz (GregTech) to Certus Quartz Crystals (AE2), but generally you shouldn't need to as all the important recipes accept either.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.217: If you need to convert them, early on you can just toss Certus Quartz (GregTech) and Small Redstone Dust (not Tiny) into Water in the world and they will form into Certus Quartz Crystals (AE2).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.218: With basic LV machines you can just run Certus Quartz (GregTech) through an Autoclave with Water to convert them into the Certus Quartz Crystals (AE2).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.219_3: if needed for more information on AE2 related things. Not everything will be covered there, but a decent amount is.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.222: A primitive multiblock structure that can smelt any ores or raw materials that can be smelted into ingots, dusts, or gems. It uses Coal, Coal Dust, Charcoal, Charcoal Dust, Coke, or Coke Dust to do so. If using Coke or Coke Dust the processing time is 75% of normal. It can also smelt some non ore material like Bricks, Bronze/Potin Dust, Silicon, Logic Chips, and some others.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.223: The Input/Output Buses will automatically push to or pull from a container that it is facing, allowing easy automation in and out of chests.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.224: It can only smelt 8 at once, not less than 8, but it will double the standard output of any ores as if they were an end or nether ore variant. Raw materials and other basic materials do not get the output boost.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.225: Because a ULV Input Bus can only hold 1 item stack, you will need 2, 1 for the fuel input and 1 for the input to smelt. For recipes that output more than 64 items like Redstone Ore -> Redstone Dust, that is too much for just 1 ULV Output Bus so you would require 2, it will split the output between the 2.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.226: They can share walls if setup properly. See images below. The Input/Output Busses and walls/floors can be shared. This is a common behavior for most multiblocks to save space and materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.229: While a Botany Pot can do the job, they are very slow and don't produce much. If you just need a slow trickle of something the Botany Pot can be fine, but if you need a lot of something, it may be better to invest in the Primitive Farm.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.230: Note the Glass in the multiblock preview can either be Bricks or Glass, the Glass is not required but can be used if you'd like.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.231: Does not require any kind of Steam, energy, or fuel source, it just takes time.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.232: The input is a non consumable item, meaning the item inserted (like a Rubber Sapling) is required, but not consumed while running.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.233: You can boost the output if you want by using Bone Meal as a secondary input, but is not required. This would be consumed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.234: &6If you are still in the Steam Age and do not have LV machines yet, you can only make the ULV Input \& Output Buses, see below.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.235: ULV Input \& Output Buses only have 1 slot each. If using ULV Input \& Output Buses, you will require as many Input Buses as input item types, and as many Output Buses as output item types. For example, a Rubber Sapling with no Bone Meal just needs the 1 ULV Input Bus, but it would require 3 ULV Output Buses, because there are 3 output item types/stacks. If you wanted to boost the recipe by adding Bone Meal with the Rubber Sapling, you would need a second ULV Input Bus for the Bone Meal, and a fourth ULV Output Bus to handle the extra items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.236: To set the Circuit value you do not need to insert it as an item. Just set the value by opening an Input Bus and clicking on the Circuit icon in the bottom left of the GUI and select the proper value there. A value of 1 is for normal recipes with no Bone Meal, and 2 is if you add Bone Meal to boost the recipe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.237: The LV Input \& Output Buses have 4 slots in them, meaning you would only require 1 of each.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.238: There is a much faster and better version a bit later on called the Greenhouse that uses energy and the recipe duration scales with the tier of Energy Hatches being used.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.239: While many of the Botany Pot recipes can be done in the Primitive Farm, not quite all can be.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.246: There are some basic early game tools that come with Silk Touch, the Silky Quartz Pickaxe, Shovel, and Axe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.247: These are basically to allow you to easily move ores where you need them for your ore generation setups, but obviously use them for whatever.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.248: Can be made with any variation of Nether Quartz and Bronze in an Alloy Smelter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.250: A Resistor is a Circuit component, Circuits tend to use things like Resistors, Diodes, Tansistors, Inductors, and many other small electronic components.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.251: They always have multiple ways to craft, unlocking with better resources which typically crafts more at a time. Always keep an eye out for a better way to craft Circuit components as you progress.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.252: Early game Paper comes from Chad, which comes from Sugar Cane either by using a Mortar or a Forge Hammer.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.254: A Vacuum Tube is "technically a Diode" and is mostly just a Circuit component, but is also technically a ULV Circuit (ultra low voltage).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.255: While they are used to make some ULV tier things, the ULV tier really isn't used much at all. While they are a ULV Circuit, they are mostly seen as a component to make LV Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.256: For now the Glass Tube is going to come from Glass Dust and a Casting Mold (Ball) in the Alloy Smelter.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.258: Circuits need Circuit Boards, different Circuit lines will need different Circuit Boards later on.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.259: For now you will need Wood Pulp, which can be obtained by putting basically anything wooden in a Macerator, logs are good as they give 6 per log.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.260: Wood Pulp in a Compressor will make a Wood Plank.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.261: You will need quite a bit of 1x Copper Wires as well for the first hand crafting method.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.262: Keep in mind there will be a much cheaper method of crafting the Resin Printed Circuit Board a bit later, once you have some power and a couple LV machines.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.264: A multiblock tank that can hold up to 500 buckets worth of fluid and can accept Steam. Be aware there is a Wooden Multiblock Tank as well, but it cannot accept Steam due to the temperature.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.265: You can feed fluids into the controller and pull fluids out of the Bronze Tank Valve. If a Bronze Tank Valve is pointing down then it will auto export into what it is connected to, like a Pipe.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.266: While you don't require a second Bronze Tank Valve for inserting the fluids as you can do so through the controller, you can have up to 2 Bronze Tank Valves if you want.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.269: GregTech offers some AOE harvesting tools.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.271: - Harvest blocks like a Pickaxe in a 3*3*1 area, hold shift to bypass the AOE effect.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.273: - Harvest blocks like a Shovel in a 3*3*1 area, hold shift to bypass the AOE effect.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.275: - Axes from GregTech have a built in ability to harvest all Logs of the same type that you are harvesting. This can be helpful, but also damaging if you have Logs in your base connected to a tree you are harvesting.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.277: - Harvest crops or till Farmland in a 5*5*3 area.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.283: A multiblock that runs items through a fluid that is placed in the center of the multiblock.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.284: The item will be coated and transform into a new item.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.285: Does not require Steam or EU, but instead consumes the fluid used to craft after 100 crafts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.290: A Steel Ingot run through the Coating Shrine will produce a Lava Coated Steel Ingot, used to upgrade the High Pressure Steam Boilers.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.292: An upgraded Steam Solid Boiler, produces 1.5 times more Steam than the High Pressure variant.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.294: An upgraded Steam Liquid Boiler, produces 1.5 times more Steam than the High Pressure variant.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.295: Creosote and Lava are the only fuel options.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.297: An upgraded Steam Solar Boiler, produces 1.5 times more Steam than the High Pressure variant.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.299: An upgraded Steam Liquid Boiler, produces 2.5 times more Steam than the Low Pressure variant.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.300: Creosote and Lava are the only fuel options.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.302: Universal Circuits are for 1 purpose, easier autocrafting Pattern management.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.303: Any Circuit can be crafted in a shapeless recipe with a Steel Plate to turn it into the Universal Circuit variant of the same tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.304: As there are multiple Circuits for the same tier, it is easier to assign Patterns the Universal Circuit variant so when you get access to a better version of the same tier Circuit, you just need to change the Pattern for the Universal Circuit instead of all your Patterns that require Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.307: The Steel Blast Furnace is basically the same as the Primitive Blast Furnace, but it can be automated by using the Steam Input Bus and Steam Output Bus. The Steel Blast Furnace does not require Steam itself to run though.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.308: Besides being able to be automated, the recipes are all 3/4 the standard durations in the Primitive Blast Furnace.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.309: It will take a decent amount of Steel Ingots to get together, but you can upgrade your Firebricks into the Primitive Smelting Bricks with Steel Dust in an Alloy Smelter so you may want to look into doing so when you can.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_steam_age.310: When you get access to the Electric Blast Furnace (EBF) you will want to switch over to that as the durations can be much faster and you don't require any type of Coal/Charcoal/Coke anymore either.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_store.2: Spend the Credits obtained from quest rewards to buy items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_store.3: &6Almost all items require you to have held one of said item before being able to buy them.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_store.4: Some exceptions are made for very basic things, things like any size of the Potin Pipes require a Potin Ingot instead of the actual Pipes, Empty Fluid Cells require either machine that can make them, and other things like this for some more basic items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_store.5: You "submit" the payment Credits by clicking on the quest objective and you will be prompted to submit the Credits, spending the Credits and allowing you to collect the reward.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_store.6: &aThese are all repeatable quests. You can buy the same thing multiple times.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.4: Kind of a replacement for Assembly Lines, making higher tiered crafting components and making lower tiered crafting components at a cheaper cost.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.5: Typically you either use the same input quantities to make double the output quantity, or less input quantities to make the same output quantity. The durations are often the same as the base recipes, while the EU voltage tier requirement is 1 step higher.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.7: You are going to want to &6make sure your infrastructure is good enough&r or this may take a very long time to get together. Such as Large Series multiblocks, high tier Parallel Hatches, UV Energy Hatches, and the EU generation/storage to handle that.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.8: The Fusion Assembler requires a Data Module programmed with a Fusion Reactor Computer MK III and uses 96 CWU/t.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.9: The Atomic Casings require a Data Module programmed with a Fusion Machine Casing MK III and uses 48 CWU/t. A minimum of 350 Atomic Casings are required in the structure. Note that you do craft 2 at a time though.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.10: The Ultimate Battery holds enough EU to last about 2.5 million days, which is almost 7000 years. 8 UHV Ultimate Capacitors are required to build the Fusion Assembler (they do not need to be full). Out of the 950+ blocks required, these 8 are the most expensive parts.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.11: The rest of the blocks needed should be "easy" to get.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uhv_age.12: Just a bit more than 950 blocks...
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.1: Requires 96 CWU/t and a UV recipe tier in the Research Station.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.3: Neutronium is the main material for the UHV Age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.6: Not too much to say here other than you are going to need quite a lot of it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.10: Liquid Americium and Liquid Naquadria will produce Liquid Neutronium in a MK III Fusion Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.11: Americium is also used for UV Electric Motors which are used in all other UV components.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.15: Liquid Lutetium and Liquid Chromium will produce Liquid Americium in a MK II Fusion Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.19: Liquid Lanthanum and Liquid Silicon will produce Liquid Lutetium in a MK I Fusion Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.23: Lanthanum Dust comes from Small Piles of Lanthanum Dust, which comes from Rare Earth in a Centrifuge.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.24: Rare Earth comes from ore processing steps using either Redstone, Monazite, Bastnasite, or Neodymium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.25: Monazite would be the most efficient, being 2 Monazite Dust to 1 Rare Earth in an LV Electrolyzer. Nether or End Monazite Ores smelt into 8 Monazite Gems and you can easily Macerate them from there.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.26: Melt the Lanthanum Dust in an Extractor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.29: Liquid Americium and Liquid Naquadria will produce Liquid Neutronium in a MK III Fusion Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.30: While you can make Liquid Naquadria with a MK III Fusion Reactor, you can also melt down the Naquadria Ingots you already have access to.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.31: Depending on your setup for Naquadria, either option might be more viable than the other.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.32: If you go the Fusion Reactor route...
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.33: Liquid Enriched Naquadah and Radon Gas in a MK III Fusion Reactor will produce Liquid Naquadria.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.34: Radon Gas can be made much faster in a MK II Fusion Reactor than standard methods, and the Mercury required can be obtained rather easily from Cinnabar Dust in a Centrifuge.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.35: Naquadria = MK III Fusion Reactor or...
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.38: The MK III Fusion Reactor, works the same as the MK I, just more powerful, and allows access to more fusion materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.40: For every Energy Hatch it has, the energy buffer increases by 40M EU, to a max of 640M EU.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.41: With the MK III Fusion Reactor you can now make Americium Plasma, the best fuel source for the Large Plasma Turbine with a base burn duration of 16 seconds.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.42: The Plutonium 241 required for the Americium Plasma is actually rather easy. The goal is to get 4 Plutonium Dust in 1.8 seconds or less, and to have the Extractor running constantly at a speed equal to or less than that, being 1.6 seconds at EV with the single block machine.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.43: See the next page for a setup good enough for enough constant Liquid Plutonium 241 to steadily produce Americium Plasma.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.45: 1 Advanced Ore Generator for Nether/End Plutonium Ore
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.50: The Furnace could be a Multi Smelter and the ZPM Macerator could be an EV Semi Perfect Macerator instead to save some energy but the energy costs for those are rather negligible anyways with the single block machines. The Centrifuge really should be a Semi Perfect version as it makes a massive difference to get to the processing speed required.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.51: The Furnace, Macerator, and Centrifuge almost run constantly, but still enough to let the Extractor run constantly at 1.5 seconds producing 144 mB of Liquid Plutonium 241. Americium Plasma needs 144 mB every 1.8 seconds. You should have a slight backup of both Plutonium 241 Dust and Liquid Plutonium 241 still as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.52: You can also use a Molecular Assembler or a Packer to turn all the Tiny Piles of Uranium Dust into proper Uranium Dust as a decent supply of Uranium Dust.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.53: The recipe for Americium Plasma does state 3.2 seconds at ZPM, however the MK III Fusion Reactor can only use UV Energy Hatches, which makes the recipe run at UV anyway.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.56: You're going to want the best Extruder you can use.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.57: 15 billion EU (and 128 Blocks of Neutronium) is not a small amount, make sure you don't run out of energy during the craft or it will restart!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.58: Hang it on your wall, you did well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.60: Even though it has eyes, it's still technically still a Circuit Board? I think?
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.62: The start of the Wetware Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.64: This is the fourth LuV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.65: This is the third ZPM Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.66: This is the second UV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.70: Data Modules are required for many UV and UV items and are programmed in the Research Station.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.71: Anything with a CWU/t rating of over 32 requires the Data Module instead of the Data Orb.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.72: &6Data Modules can only be placed in Data Access Hatches that are part of an active Data Bank.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.75: The UV Superconductor, has a loss of 0 EU per block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.77: The fourth and final tier of Wafer material.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.78: Cuts into 96 Neutronium-doped Wafers at a time and has better output ratios for Laser Engraving than the third tier.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.80: Just like the other SoC types, the HASoC can be used to make the Wetware Processors much cheaper and faster than the standard recipes. This does require a UV recipe tier in the Circuit Assembler though.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.81: Also used in some other recipes besides just Circuits.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.83: The only new unique Wafer that comes only from the Neutronium-doped Wafer. Used to make the HASoC.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.85: An upgrade to the Auto Maintenance Hatch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.86: The Cleaning Maintenance Hatch allows a multiblock to perform recipes that require a Cleanroom (while not being in a Cleanroom), and is still an Auto Maintenance Hatch as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.88: A Quantum Star infused with Liquid Neutronium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.89: Used in UV Emitters, UV Sensors, and UV Field Generators.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.91: Used to process recipes with a UV requirement.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.93: The UHV Superconductor, has a loss of 0 EU per block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.94: Also used to make the UHV Energy Hatch, UHV Dynamo Hatch, Rotary Hearth Furnace, and Bulk Blast Chiller.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.96: Can accept more than 1 Computation Data Transmission Hatch and Computation Data Reception Hatch, which allows multiple HPCAs to feed into the Network Switch, then send out as a higher combined CWU/t in a single Optical Fiber Cable.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.97: The HPCA Bridge Component must be installed in an HPCA to allow connecting to a Network Switch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.99: Used to craft UV Energy Hatches, UV Dynamo Hatches, and the Fusion Machine Casing MK III.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.101: Another upgrade to the Energy Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_uv_age.103: Another upgrade to the Energy Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.1: The first Circuit not created in the Circuit Assembler since the first MV Circuit. Now it's all Assembly Line production.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.2: The Data Orb for the Crystal Processor Mainframe is programmed using a Crystal Processor Supercomputer in the Research Station and requires a minimum of 16 CWU/t. This is probably the first time you need to reconfigure the HPCA for a higher CWU/t.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.3: Using 4 HPCA Active Cooling Components and 4 HPCA Computation Components can reach the 16 CWU/t required with the proper cooling amount as well.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.4: Be sure to supply the HPCA with PCB Coolant as the HPCA Active Cooling Components are not passive and require the PCB Coolant pumped in through an Input Hatch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.5: You will also need to have 2 ZPM Energy Hatches or a 4A ZPM Energy Hatch on the HPCA as it requires more EU/t for the computation than previous recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.7: Darmstadtium is the main material for the UV Age.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.9: Darmstadtium is a fusion material that comes from Arsenic Vapor and Liquid Ruthenium in a MK II Fusion Reactor.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.10: The first tiered ingot to be finalized in a Fluid Solidifier, and also requiring UV Circuits before the ingot.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.11: Being the main material for the UV age, this is basically going to have to be a steady production.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.15: The MK II Fusion Reactor, works the same as the MK I, just more powerful, and allows access to more fusion materials.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.16: &aCan only accept ZPM, and UV Energy Hatches.&r
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.17: For every Energy Hatch it has, the energy buffer increases by 20M EU, to a max of 320M EU.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.20: Basically just used for the Raw Growth Medium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.21: Can also be used in the Raw Crystal Chip production, with an 85% chance of an output. Not a bad alternitive to Europium if you want to lean away from the Europium for that process.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.25: Most of this mixture is pretty straight forward, but you may want to look into the Meat Box multiblock if you need a steady source of meat for the Mince Meat and don't want a passive mob farm.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.26: This is the least scientific thing I've ever seen.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.29: Ever wanted to add radioactive elements to living Bacteria? How else would you create Stem Cells?
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.33: The start of creating Stem Cells, and in turn the Sterilized Growth Medium, both are used in making Circuits so a steady supply will be required.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.34: This whole process up to Stem Cells will require a Sterile Cleanroom so prepare for that.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.35: Making Bacteria is actually a very basic process, just make sure to do so in a Sterile Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.36: Biomass is even easier and can be done anywhere, it's basically just some plant material with Water.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.40: Just heat up the Raw Growth Medium and try not to vomit to get some Sterilized Growth Medium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.41: Used to make Stem Cells, Wetware Circuit Boards, and Neuro Processing Units, which are all part of Circuits, so a steady supply will be required.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.45: Does not need to be in a Sterile Cleanroom, just a regular Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.46: Used to make the Data Module, Neuro Processing Unit, Wetware Processor Assembly Circuit, Wetware Processor Supercomputer Circuit, and Energy Cluster.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.47: At least they don't have eyes yet...
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.48: Used in making the Neuro Processing Unit for the Wetware Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.52: The start of the Crystal Processor Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.53: While not required, it's highly advised to use the Crystal SoC method. It requires a ZPM Energy Hatch and the Large Circuit Assembling Facility, but that is all obtainable before you make the first Crystal Processor anyhow.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.54: This is the fourth IV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.55: This is the third LuV Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.56: Used in an LuV Circuit Assembler or higher to make the Crystal Processor Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.57: While you can make the Multi-layer Fiber-Reinforced Printed Circuit Boards much earlier, they see no use until now.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.59: The Multi-layer Fiber-Reinforced Circuit Board is used to make both the Crystal Processor Circuit line, and the Wetware Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.61: This is the second ZPM Circuit!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.62: A more advanced multiblock version of the Scanner, required for programming Data Orbs and Data Modules.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.63: The Research Station requires computation which is measured as CWU/t, and is provided by the High Performance Computation Array (HPCA) using Optical Fiber Cables.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.64: The Object Holder on the Research Station is what holds a Data Orb or Data Module to be programmed and also where you place the item used to program.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.65: &6A Computation Data Transmission Hatch can only supply 1 Computation Data Reception Hatch.&r The Network Switch available a bit later can have more than 1 of each, which allows feeding multiple HPCAs into the Network Switch and sending out as a larger CWU/t. Due to the limitations on how many HPCA components can be used in a single HPCA and the higher CWU/t required for later Data Modules, you will eventually need the Network Switch to combine the CWU/t from more than 1 HPCA together.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.66: The HPCA requires EU and cooling to run and provide computation (CWU).
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.67: The HPCA allows 9 slots for HPCA components (multiblock parts) that alter how it works. There are 6 different HPCA blocks that can be used in the 9 block slots with different CWU/t, cooling ratings, and behaviors. They all have HPCA in the name so just search EMI for "HPCA" and see the available blocks and what they each do in the tooltips.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.68: Some blocks provide a small amount of passive cooling. Some blocks provide more cooling at the cost of PCB Coolant. Some blocks provide CWU/t while requiring different levels of cooling. There are also filler blocks that do nothing but help complete the multiblock if you don't require more of the others. And there is also the HPCA Bridge Component which allows connecting to a Network Switch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.69: The recipes for the Data Orb or Data Module programming in the Research Station display a minimum CWU/t value which must be provided by the HPCA and can be transferred from the Computation Data Transmission Hatch from the HPCA to the Computation Data Reception Hatch on the Research Station using Optical Fiber Cables.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.70: Computation (CWU) cannot be stored and must be generated and sent directly as needed.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.73: There are multiple recipes for the Raw Crystal Chip, but to start you need the Europium and either Equisite Olivine or Exquisite Emerald. There is a 25% chance of making the Raw Crystal Chip with this method so it may take a few tries.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.74: However putting a Raw Crystal Chip in a Forge Hammer will break it into 9 Raw Crystal Chip Parts. Then you can turn 1 Raw Crystal Chip Part back into a full Raw Crystal Chip again. Using Liquid Europium and the Raw Crystal Chip Part is a 100% chance for the Raw Crystal Chip. So once you have 1 Raw Crystal Chip, you can essentially replicate them in a loop.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.75: Ideally you will want a system that always stores some excess to be used again in making more, you don't want to use the last one you have.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.76: This does need to be done in a Cleanroom so the Semi Perfect Crystallization Chamber will not be an option, but the Large Crystallization Chamber can be used.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.78: A bit of an odd recipe, either Olivine or Emerald Plates and the Raw Crystal Chip in an HV EBF with HSS-G Coils and Helium Gas will make the Engraved Crystal Chip.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.80: An LuV Laser Engraver in a Cleanroom will finally make the Crystal CPU for use in the new Crystal Processor Circuit line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.81: See the Crystal SoC quest above for an easier and cheaper method of making the Crystal Processors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.83: Sterilizing Filter Casings can replace the original Filter Casings in the ceiling of the Cleanroom, making it a Sterile Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.84: The Sterilizing Filter Casings are incredibly expensive. You may want to build a tall and thin room instead of a 15*15 wide.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.85: Going forward many things will require the Sterile Cleanroom.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.87: An upgraded Superconducting Coil Block, used in the MK II and MK III Fusion Reactors.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.89: When finally making the Stem Cells you will get some Bacterial Sludge back, but first you need to make some by mixing
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.90: Why not turn the Bacteria to a sludge?
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.93: The ZPM Superconductor, has a loss of 0 EU per block.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.94: Also used in making the Mk II Fusion Reactor, and even the ZPM Field Generator, which is required for the Rotary Hearth Furnace, and the Energy Cluster which eventually also leads to the Ultimate Battery.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.96: Liquid Gallium and Radon Gas in a MK I Fusion Reactor will produce Liquid Duranium for further fusion reactions.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.100: Liquid Duranium and Liquid Titanium in a MK II Fusion Reactor will produce Liquid Tritanium.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.104: Liquid Tritanium can be solidified for use as a metal.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.105: Tritanium is used for quite a bit, including Tritanium Coils, Sterilizing Filter Casings, MK III Fusion Reactor Casings, many UV crafting components and more.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.109: Another upgrade to the Energy Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.111: Used to craft ZPM Energy Hatches, ZPM Dynamo Hatches, and the Fusion Machine Casing MK II.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.113: Used to process recipes with an LuV requirement.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.115: You can get Enriched Naquadah Dust from ore processing steps for Naquadah Ore, or from the Naquadah Line.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.116: It may be easier to just use the Enriched Naquadah Dust but having the extra produced from the Naquadah Line may not hurt to have.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.117_3: if you want to see the secondary way to make Enriched Naquadah Ingots.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.118: Enriched Naquadah Dust or the Naquadah Line!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.119: Compared to the LuV Dual Input Hatch, the extra tank and extra item slots makes the ZPM Dual Input Hatch much more viable for most Assembler and LCR recipes.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.121: Nothing too special about the ZPM Input Bus compared to other versions other than the inventory size, but used to make the ZPM Dual Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.123: Nothing too special about the ZPM Input Hatch compared to other versions other than the tank size, but used to make the ZPM Dual Hatches.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.125: Just like the ASoC from earlier, the Crystal SoC can be used to make the Crystal Processors much cheaper and faster.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.126: Requires a ZPM Laser Engraver in a Cleanroom, but you can tier skip with the Large Engraving Laser with LuV Energy Hatches, or just use 1 ZPM Energy Hatch if you went that route first. The ZPM Energy Hatch would be required to make the Crystal Processor with the Crystal SoC before access to UV Circuits anyways.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.127: Requires a ZPM Circuit Assembler in a Cleanroom, but same as above, you can make the ZPM Energy Hatch for the Large Circuit Assembling Facility and start with the better recipe, skipping the need for the Advanced SMD components and the Nano CPU Chips.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.129: Required for making the the Fusion Reactor MK III, Fusion Machine Casing MK III, Energy Cluster, HPCA Advanced Computation Component, and the UV Field Generator.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.130: Going to need quite a few...
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.133: Required to generate more computation in the HPCA.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.134: This is the most CWU/t you can generate in a single block. To reach higher levels that is required by any configuration of these in an HPCA, you need to use the Network Switch.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.136: Can perform up to 64 recipes at once, as long as you have the EU to support it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.137: Depending on the recipes you may also need a much larger Input Bus to handle the amount of items.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.141: You will need the Bulk Blast Chiller to keep up with it.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.146: Basically required to keep up with the Rotary Hearth Furnace.
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.147: Not as big, but still as useful!
sky_greg.quests.chapters_zpm_age.151: You will need the Bulk Blast Chiller to keep up with it.
